rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its rating systems provide a meaningful assessment of obligor and transaction characteristics.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Validation covers design, rating process and assignment of obligors to grades, but the policy does not explicitly require a check that the system gives a meaningful assessment of obligor and transaction characteristics (transaction side is missing).

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its rating systems provide a meaningful differentiation of risk.
rows.quote: **Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Annual discriminatory power assessment together with rating distribution stability checks addresses meaningful risk differentiation.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its rating systems provide accurate and consistent quantitative estimates of risk.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years, using binomial and Jeffreys tests.
rows.rationale: Calibration back-testing exists for PD, LGD and CCF, but PD back-testing is only biennial and the policy does not state an explicit consistency requirement; it is also weakened by the exclusion of external benchmarks.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the IRB requirements, including those for own LGD and conversion factor estimates, also to rating systems or models purchased from a third-party vendor.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address purchased third-party vendor models or apply IRB requirements to them.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall ensure the model has good predictive power.
rows.quote: **Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Validation assesses predictive power through annual discriminatory power and back-testing of the model.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that own funds requirements are not distorted as a result of the use of the model.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to ensure own funds requirements are not distorted by model use.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall ensure the model input variables form a reasonable and effective basis for the resulting predictions.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Model design is validated generally, but there is no explicit check that input variables form a reasonable and effective basis for predictions.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall ensure the model does not have material biases.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Back-testing detects deviations (bias) indirectly, but material bias is not explicitly checked as a requirement.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall ensure there is a functional link between the inputs and the outputs of the model, which may be determined through expert judgement where appropriate.
rows.rationale: No clause requires a check of a functional link between model inputs and outputs.

rows.obligation: The institution using pooled data shall remain responsible for the integrity of its rating systems.
rows.rationale: The policy does not indicate that the bank uses pooled data.

rows.obligation: The institution using pooled data shall maintain sufficient in-house understanding of its rating systems, including the ability to effectively monitor and audit the rating process.
rows.rationale: The policy does not indicate that the bank uses pooled data.

rows.obligation: The management body or a designated committee thereof shall approve all material aspects of the rating and estimation processes.
rows.quote: New rating systems are approved by the MRC after initial validation. Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: The MRC approves new systems, but material changes are approved by the Head of Model Development, so not all material aspects are approved by the management body or its committee.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall approve all material aspects of the rating and estimation processes.
rows.quote: New rating systems are approved by the MRC after initial validation. Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: The CRO-chaired MRC approves new systems, but material changes are approved by a department head rather than senior management, so not all material aspects are covered.

rows.obligation: The management body or its designated committee shall possess a general understanding of the institution's rating systems and detailed comprehension of the associated management reports.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The Management Board receives reports but the policy does not require a general understanding of rating systems or detailed comprehension of the management reports.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall possess a general understanding of the institution's rating systems and detailed comprehension of the associated management reports.
rows.rationale: No clause requires senior management to understand the rating systems or the associated management reports.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall have a good understanding of the rating systems designs and operations.
rows.quote: It is responsible for ensuring that the Bank's rating systems are sound and appropriately validated.
rows.rationale: Management Board receives the annual validation report, but the policy does not require senior management to understand rating system design and operations (no training or briefing requirement).

rows.obligation: Senior management shall ensure on an ongoing basis that the rating systems are operating properly.
rows.quote: It is responsible for ensuring that the Bank's rating systems are sound and appropriately validated.
rows.rationale: Responsibility and annual reporting are stated, but ongoing assurance that systems operate properly is only annual and not tied to senior management.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall be responsible for the design or selection, implementation, oversight and performance of the rating systems.
rows.rationale: Allocating design, implementation, oversight and performance responsibility to the credit risk control unit is a rating-system governance matter for another document, not the validation policy.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall actively participate in the design or selection, implementation and validation of models used in the rating process.
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development, with a dotted reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer for validation matters.
rows.rationale: Validation sits within the development department, and the policy gives no role to a credit risk control unit in design/selection, implementation and validation of models.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall oversee and supervise models used in the rating process.
rows.rationale: The policy does not assign a credit risk control unit any oversight or supervision of models in the rating process.

rows.obligation: The institution outsourcing tasks under Article 190(3) shall ensure that competent authorities have access to all relevant information from the third party necessary for examining compliance.
rows.rationale: Competent authority access to outsourced third parties belongs in an outsourcing policy, and the validation policy does not describe outsourcing.

rows.obligation: The institution outsourcing tasks under Article 190(3) shall ensure that competent authorities may perform on-site examinations at the third party to the same extent as within the institution.
rows.rationale: On-site examination rights at third parties belong in an outsourcing policy, not in the validation policy.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 114
rows.obligation: The institution using the IRB Approach should adopt adequate mechanisms and procedures to ensure the definition of default is implemented and used correctly.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Validation checks consistent and correct application of the default definition, serving as a mechanism to ensure correct implementation and use.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 114
rows.obligation: The management body, or a committee designated by it, and senior management shall approve the definition of default and the scope of its application in accordance with Article 189(1) of Regulation (EU) 575/2013.
rows.rationale: The policy sets out the default definition in §7 but names no approval by the management body or committee and senior management of the definition and its scope.

rows.obligation: When complementing statistical models with human judgement, the institution should assess the modelling assumptions and whether the selected risk drivers contribute to the risk assessment in line with their economic meaning.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention human judgement or require validation to assess modelling assumptions and risk driver economic meaning.

rows.obligation: When complementing statistical models with human judgement, the institution should analyse the impact of the human judgement on model performance.
rows.rationale: No requirement to analyse the impact of human judgement on model performance.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that any form of human judgement is properly justified.
rows.rationale: No requirement that human judgement be justified or that validation checks such justification.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have robust arrangements, mechanisms and processes for validating its rating systems, with appropriate personnel responsible for the validation function.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Validation processes and staffing are described, but the validation function lacks independence from development (§4.1), so the arrangements are not fully robust.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall use adequate methods and procedures.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: Excluding external data and benchmarks is an inadequate validation method, as the validation function should use such comparisons.

rows.obligation: Senior management and the management body shall fulfil their role in internal governance and oversight of the rating systems.
rows.quote: The **Management Board** approves this Policy and receives the annual validation report.
rows.rationale: Management Board and MRC roles are described, but material changes are approved by the Head of Model Development without senior management/management body approval (§3.4), weakening oversight.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall fulfil its required role in accordance with Article 16.
rows.quote: Validation is performed by the Model Validation team.
rows.rationale: The policy sets up a validation team but does not define a credit risk control unit or give it the Article 16 role, and the team's reporting line to the Head of Model Development weakens its independence.

rows.obligation: The institution shall take decisions on validation conclusions, findings and recommendations at the appropriate management level.
rows.quote: decides on the use of models with open findings
rows.rationale: The MRC, chaired by the CRO, decides on models with open findings and on measures for overdue high findings, and the Management Board receives the annual report, so decisions sit at an appropriate management level.

rows.obligation: The institution shall consistently reflect its decision-making process, hierarchy, reporting lines and levels of responsibility in the minutes of its internal bodies.
rows.rationale: How the minutes of internal bodies reflect decision-making and hierarchy is a general governance matter and not for a validation policy.

rows.obligation: The management body or the committee designated by it shall approve all relevant policies relating to the design and implementation of rating systems and application of the IRB Approach, including policies on rating assignment, risk parameter estimation and validation processes.
rows.quote: Changes are approved by the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The Management Board approves this validation policy, but the policy does not cover approval of the policies on rating assignment and risk parameter estimation.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall approve all relevant policies relating to the design and implementation of rating systems and application of the IRB Approach, including policies on rating assignment, risk parameter estimation and validation processes.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention senior management approval of IRB policies.

rows.obligation: The management body or the committee designated by it shall approve the risk parameters of all rating systems used in internal risk management processes and in the calculation of own funds requirements.
rows.quote: New rating systems are approved by the MRC after initial validation.
rows.rationale: The MRC approves new rating systems, but the policy says nothing about approving the risk parameters of all rating systems, and material changes are approved only by the Head of Model Development.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall approve the risk parameters of all rating systems used in internal risk management processes and in the calculation of own funds requirements.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require senior management to approve risk parameters.

rows.obligation: The management body or the committee designated by it shall set, by formal decision, an appropriate organisational structure for the sound implementation of the rating systems.
rows.rationale: Setting the organisational structure for implementing rating systems by formal decision belongs in general governance documents.

rows.obligation: The management body or the committee designated by it shall approve by formal decision the specification of the acceptable level of risk, taking into account the institution's internal rating system scheme.
rows.rationale: Specifying the acceptable level of risk is a general governance and risk appetite matter, not a validation matter.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall have a good understanding of all rating systems of the institution, their design and operation, the IRB Approach requirements and the institution's approach to meeting them.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement on senior management's understanding of the rating systems.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall notify the management body or the committee designated by it of material changes to or exceptions from established policies that materially impact the operations of the institution's rating systems.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: The MRC is informed of material changes, but there is no requirement to notify the management body of exceptions from policies, and the notification comes from the Head of Model Development, not from senior management.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall be in a position to ensure on an ongoing basis the good functioning of the rating systems.
rows.quote: It is responsible for ensuring that the Bank's rating systems are sound and appropriately validated.
rows.rationale: The policy assigns responsibility for sound systems to the Management Board and gives it annual reporting, but does not require senior management to ensure ongoing good functioning.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the credit risk control unit or units are functional and adequate for their tasks.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Adequate staffing is required for validation only, and the policy does not address the credit risk control unit's functionality and adequacy as a whole.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the head of the credit risk control unit, or the heads of such units, are part of the senior management.
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development, with a dotted reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer for validation matters.
rows.rationale: The validation team reports to the Head of Model Development, not to a head who is part of senior management, which is incompatible with the requirement.

rows.obligation: The institution shall organise the credit risk management function taking into account the principles set out in Article 76(5) of Directive 2013/36/EU.
rows.rationale: Organising the credit risk management function under Article 76(5) of Directive 2013/36/EU belongs in general risk governance documents.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the credit risk control unit or units are proportionate to the nature, size and degree of complexity of its business and organisational structure, in particular to the complexity of the rating systems and their implementation.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address proportionality of the credit risk control unit to the nature, size and complexity of the business and rating systems.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the credit risk control unit or units have adequate resources and experienced and qualified personnel to undertake all relevant activities.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory. Staffing and skills are reviewed annually as part of the validation plan.
rows.rationale: The policy requires sufficient resources and expertise for the validation team, though it does not cover the credit risk control unit beyond validation.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall be responsible for the design or selection, implementation, oversight and performance of the rating systems, including the areas of responsibility listed in Article 190(2) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013.
rows.rationale: The policy does not assign the credit risk control unit responsibility for design/selection, implementation, oversight and performance of rating systems, and it places design with Model Development.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should have a model risk management framework in place that allows it to identify, understand and manage its model risk for internal models across the group.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: A model risk oversight body and group scope (subsidiaries) exist, but there is no full framework for identifying, understanding and managing model risk.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should have guidelines on identifying and mitigating areas where measurement uncertainty and model deficiencies are known to exist, according to their materiality, considering qualitative aspects such as data deficiencies, model misuse or implementation errors.
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A) and assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate.
rows.rationale: MoC and findings handle deficiencies, but only data and methodology deficiencies are covered, not qualitative ones like model misuse or implementation errors, and there is no materiality-based guideline.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should apply its methodology for identifying and mitigating measurement uncertainty and model deficiencies consistently across the group (e.g. in subsidiaries or regions).
rows.quote: The Policy applies to the Bank and to all subsidiaries that use the Bank's IRB rating systems.
rows.rationale: The policy applies group-wide, but there is no explicit requirement to apply the deficiency/uncertainty methodology consistently across the group.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should have guidelines and methodologies for the qualitative and/or quantitative assessment and measurement of the institution's model risk.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Model risk is assessed in reporting and tiering, but no methodology for qualitative or quantitative measurement of model risk is defined.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should have guidelines with respect to the model life cycle.
rows.quote: **Initial validation** is performed for every new rating system before the Bank applies for permission to use it or before its first use for own funds requirements.
rows.rationale: Some life-cycle stages (initial approval, regular validation, material changes) are addressed, but there is no complete model life cycle guideline.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should define roles and responsibilities within the model risk management framework, including which unit(s) are in charge of or involved in independent reviews of risk estimates.
rows.quote: Validation is performed by the Model Validation team.
rows.rationale: Roles of the Management Board, MRC, owners, developers and the validation unit responsible for independent review are defined.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should define and document the appropriate levels of skills, capabilities and expertise required for each stakeholder group (including senior management), commensurate with its model risk and each stakeholder's duties.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Skill levels are addressed only for the validation team, not for each stakeholder group including senior management.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should devise appropriate training programmes for all stakeholder groups so that the required skill levels are reached and then maintained.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no training programmes for stakeholder groups.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should regularly review the skills, capabilities and expertise levels and training programmes to help ensure stakeholders can consistently manage model risk.
rows.quote: Staffing and skills are reviewed annually as part of the validation plan.
rows.rationale: Skills are reviewed annually but only for the validation team and with no mention of training programmes or other stakeholders.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 14
rows.obligation: The institution should clearly define the roles and responsibilities of its management body and senior management with regard to internal models and in relation to each risk type.
rows.quote: The **Management Board** approves this Policy and receives the annual validation report. It is responsible for ensuring that the Bank's rating systems are sound and appropriately validated.
rows.rationale: Management Board roles are defined for validation, but senior management roles are not and responsibilities are not set out for internal models in relation to each risk type.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 16
rows.obligation: The institution should assess the appropriateness of designated committees of the management body to ensure they provide adequate support for effective decision-making, in particular for decisions on material aspects of internal models.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require assessing the appropriateness of committees of the management body to support decision-making on internal models.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 16
rows.obligation: The management body should give model governance committees a mandate that clearly defines their tasks and authority.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The MRC tasks are described, but there is no formal mandate from the management body defining its tasks and authority, including its limits.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 16
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that the designated committee is chaired by a member of the management body.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The designated committee is chaired by the CRO, and the policy does not state that the CRO is a member of the management body, so the chairing requirement is not shown to be met.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 17
rows.obligation: The institution should be able to identify which individuals constitute its senior management with respect to the credit, market and counterparty credit risk Pillar I model frameworks.
rows.rationale: The policy does not identify or define who constitutes senior management for the credit risk model framework.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 24
rows.obligation: The institution shall adequately staff the validation function in line with the proportionality principle.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Staffing adequacy is required and reviewed annually, but there is no reference to proportionality to the nature, size and complexity of the models.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 23
rows.obligation: The institution shall treat materiality as an essential consideration in model risk management.
rows.quote: Models are classified into three tiers based on the exposure covered and the risk-weighted exposure amounts. The tier determines the depth of validation work, not whether a model is validated.
rows.rationale: Materiality-based tiering explicitly drives the depth of validation, treating materiality as a key consideration.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 23
rows.obligation: The institution shall subject rating systems it classifies as material to particular scrutiny.
rows.quote: The tier determines the depth of validation work, not whether a model is validated.
rows.rationale: Higher tiers receive deeper validation work, which amounts to particular scrutiny of material models.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 24
rows.obligation: The institution shall assess and determine the materiality of its rating systems.
rows.quote: Models are classified into three tiers based on the exposure covered and the risk-weighted exposure amounts.
rows.rationale: A materiality classification exists, but the policy does not say who assesses and determines it or give the criteria and thresholds.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 24
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that material rating systems at least include the rating systems covering material types of exposure.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require that material rating systems include those covering material types of exposure, and its tiers are based only on exposure and RWA.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 24
rows.obligation: The institution shall review its classification of rating systems by materiality on a regular basis.
rows.rationale: No regular review of the tier classification is required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 26
rows.obligation: The management body (or a committee designated by it) shall approve material aspects of all rating and estimation processes.
rows.quote: New rating systems are approved by the MRC after initial validation. Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: The MRC approves new systems, but material changes are approved by the Head of Model Development with only an after-the-fact notification, and other material aspects of rating and estimation processes are not covered.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 26
rows.obligation: Senior management shall approve material aspects of all rating and estimation processes.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: Senior management approval is limited to material changes and does not extend to all material aspects of rating and estimation processes, and senior management is not defined.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 28
rows.obligation: The institution shall define which policies require approval by both the management body and senior management and clarify this in their respective mandates.
rows.rationale: The policy does not define which policies need approval by both the management body and senior management, nor clarify this in mandates.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 28
rows.obligation: The management body and senior management shall both approve risk management policies that could have a material impact on the institution's rating systems and risk estimates.
rows.quote: Changes are approved by the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The Management Board approves this policy, but there is no joint approval by senior management and no coverage of other risk management policies with material impact.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 28
rows.obligation: The management body and senior management shall both approve policies covering the risk of a third-party provider for model-related tasks ceasing to operate (IT infrastructure and contingency planning).
rows.rationale: Policies on third-party provider failure, IT infrastructure and contingency planning belong in outsourcing or IT governance documents, not in a validation policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 29
rows.obligation: Senior management shall provide notice to the management body or a designated committee of material changes or exceptions from established policies.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for senior management to notify the management body or a committee of material changes or exceptions from policies.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 29
rows.obligation: The institution shall be able to demonstrate which material changes or exceptions from established policies are communicated to the management body or its designated committee, and how.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no mechanism to demonstrate which material changes or exceptions from policies are communicated to the management body or a designated committee.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 29
rows.obligation: The institution shall have a policy in place which defines material changes or exceptions from established policies.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: The policy treats material changes in approval governance but does not define what is a material change or an exception from established policies.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The management body shall possess a general understanding of the rating systems.
rows.quote: It is responsible for ensuring that the Bank's rating systems are sound and appropriately validated.
rows.rationale: The Management Board receives the annual validation report but the policy does not require a general understanding of the rating systems.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: Senior management shall have a good understanding of the rating systems designs and operations.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no requirement on senior management's understanding of rating system design and operations.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution should be able to provide evidence of the processes it uses to improve and maintain the management body's and senior management's understanding of the rating systems, including those implemented after receiving IRB permission.
rows.rationale: No processes or evidence for maintaining management body and senior management understanding are described.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 38
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure the format and content of its processes for building understanding (e.g. workshops, seminars, training on IRB models) match the roles and responsibilities of the management body and senior management, in particular those related to model approval.
rows.rationale: Training and workshop content for management belongs in a governance or training document, not a validation policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 38
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure an adequate balance between collective and individual knowledge in the management body.
rows.rationale: Management body composition and knowledge balance is a general governance charter matter.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 38
rows.obligation: The institution should maintain adequate internal knowledge of outsourced tasks where third parties are involved.
rows.rationale: Internal knowledge of outsourced tasks belongs in an outsourcing policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 39
rows.obligation: The institution shall not rely only on reporting or monitoring to ensure the management body and senior management have an adequate understanding of the rating systems.
rows.rationale: The policy only provides reporting (annual report) and has no measure of understanding beyond reporting, nor addresses this expectation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 40
rows.obligation: The management body or designated committee should be able to hold an objective debate on, and challenge, the rating systems, in particular for approval of material changes or the escalation process.
rows.quote: oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The MRC has an oversight and decision role but the policy does not state it can hold objective debate and challenge on rating systems and material changes.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 40
rows.obligation: The management body or designated committee should be able to discuss the outcomes, use, strengths and limitations of the IRB models.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Results are reported to the Board but no discussion of outcomes, use, strengths and limitations is required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 40
rows.obligation: The management body or designated committee should make evidence of challenge and debate visible in the minutes of its meetings (best practice).
rows.rationale: The policy does not require minutes to evidence challenge and debate.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 42
rows.obligation: The institution should have a clear written mandate for its CRCU clarifying its roles and responsibilities, aligned to the responsibilities in Article 190(2) of the CRR.
rows.rationale: A written CRCU mandate aligned to Article 190(2) belongs in a governance charter rather than the validation policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 42
rows.obligation: The institution should determine which units are responsible for which subset of CRCU tasks, especially model design and development and ongoing monitoring of the rating systems.
rows.quote: Model developers in the Model Development & Analytics department design, estimate, calibrate and document the models.
rows.rationale: Roles for development and validation are allocated but ongoing monitoring responsibility and CRCU task allocation are not defined.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 43
rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall ensure the satisfactory performance of the rating systems and their ongoing maintenance.
rows.quote: Model owners in the business and risk departments are responsible for the performance and use of their models.
rows.rationale: Performance responsibility is assigned to model owners and validation is annual, but no unit is tasked with ensuring satisfactory performance and ongoing maintenance of the rating systems.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 49
rows.obligation: The validation function shall retain responsibility for validation tasks at the level at which the rating system is approved.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the level at which validation responsibility is retained, such as for subsidiaries using the Bank's systems.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 58
rows.obligation: Senior management shall ensure, on an ongoing basis, that the rating systems are operating properly.
rows.quote: It is responsible for ensuring that the Bank's rating systems are sound and appropriately validated.
rows.rationale: The Management Board is made responsible for ensuring rating systems are sound and validated, and receives the annual validation report (§3.1, §14.2), which matches the duty on senior management to ensure they operate properly.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 58
rows.obligation: Senior management should be directly involved (e.g. by chairing the committee) in the follow-up process on validation findings, at least for material rating systems.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The MRC, chaired by the CRO (senior management), decides on models with open findings and on measures for overdue high findings, so senior management is directly involved in follow-up.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 58
rows.obligation: The institution should have an escalation process up to management body level for conflicts between the validation function, the CRCU and/or business units.
rows.rationale: The policy has no escalation process up to management body level for conflicts between the validation function, the CRCU and/or business units.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should follow its internal validation policy when carrying out validations.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require that validations be carried out in accordance with the internal validation policy itself, and it has no compliance requirement or check.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure internal ratings and default and loss estimates used in own funds calculations, and the associated systems and processes, play an essential role in risk management, decision-making, credit approval, internal capital allocation and corporate governance.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Validation covers the use of the model, but the policy does not require checking that ratings play an essential role in risk management, decision-making, credit approval, capital allocation and governance.

rows.obligation: The institution shall complement the statistical model by human judgement and human oversight to review model-based assignments and to ensure that the models are used appropriately.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: Validation looks at the rating process and assignment, but the policy does not require human judgement and oversight to complement the model or validation of how it is applied.

rows.obligation: The institution shall design review procedures to aim at finding and limiting errors associated with model weaknesses.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for review procedures designed to find and limit errors arising from model weaknesses.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure human judgements take into account all relevant information not considered by the model.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address human judgements or whether they take into account all relevant information not considered by the model.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 114
rows.obligation: The institution should use the definition of default consistently for own funds requirements calculation and in internal risk management, at least in monitoring of exposures and internal reporting to senior management and the management body.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Consistency is checked across models, portfolios and estimation data, but not between own funds calculation and internal risk management (monitoring, internal reporting to senior management).

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: Internal audit should include in its general risk assessment its opinion on the use of the models, including whether rating systems play an essential role in risk management, decision-making, credit approval, internal capital allocation and corporate governance.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: Internal audit reviews only the validation team, with no opinion on the use of the rating systems or their essential role in risk management and governance.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution shall complement the statistical model by human judgement and human oversight to review model-based assignments and ensure that the models are used appropriately.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: Assignment is assessed, but there is no requirement for human judgement and oversight to complement the statistical model.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should assess the impact of the application of human judgement on risk differentiation capability (e.g. discriminatory power).
rows.rationale: The policy does not require assessing the impact of human judgement on risk differentiation or discriminatory power.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have a credit risk control unit responsible for its rating systems that is appropriately independent and free from undue influence.
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development, with a dotted reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer for validation matters.
rows.rationale: Validation sits inside the model development department and reports to the head of development, so it is not appropriately independent or free from undue influence.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall be independent from the personnel and management functions responsible for originating or renewing exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address independence of the validation/control unit from the functions originating or renewing exposures.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall report directly to senior management.
rows.quote: reports to the Head of Model Development, with a dotted reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer for validation matters
rows.rationale: The primary reporting line is to the Head of Model Development rather than directly to senior management; the CRO line is only dotted.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall be independent.
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development
rows.rationale: Validation is embedded in the development department, which is incompatible with an independent validation function.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall be independent from the personnel and management function responsible for originating or renewing exposures and for model design or development.
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development
rows.rationale: Validation is part of and reports to the model development management, contrary to required independence from model design and development.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the staff performing the validation function are different from the staff responsible for design and development of the rating system and from the staff responsible for the credit risk control function.
rows.quote: Validators do not validate models they have developed themselves.
rows.rationale: Only prevents validators validating their own models; does not require staff to be different from the development staff generally or from the credit risk control function.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall report directly to senior management.
rows.quote: reports to the Head of Model Development, with a dotted reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer for validation matters.
rows.rationale: Validation reports to the Head of Model Development, not directly to senior management.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the validation function has adequate resources, including experienced and qualified personnel, where it is organisationally separate from the credit risk control unit and the units report to different senior management members.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Resources and expertise are required, but the policy does not frame this for the separate-unit/different-senior-management case and covers only expertise and not experienced, qualified personnel fully.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that remuneration of validation staff and senior managers is not linked to the performance of credit risk control tasks or of originating or renewing exposures, where the validation and credit risk control units are separate and report to different senior management members.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement on remuneration of validation staff and senior managers.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the validation function has adequate resources, including experienced and qualified personnel, where the validation and credit risk control units are separate but report to the same senior management member.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Staffing sufficiency is addressed, but only expertise, not explicitly experienced and qualified personnel overall.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that remuneration of validation staff and senior managers is not linked to credit risk control tasks or to originating or renewing exposures, where both units report to the same senior management member.
rows.rationale: No remuneration safeguards for validation staff are stated.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure no undue influence is exercised on the validation function's conclusions, findings and recommendations, where both units report to the same senior management member.
rows.rationale: The policy has no provision against undue influence on validation conclusions, findings and recommendations.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that, where there is no separate validation unit, the validation function has adequate resources, including experienced and qualified personnel, to perform its tasks.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Addresses resource and expertise sufficiency but not explicitly experienced and qualified personnel to perform all tasks.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that, where there is no separate validation unit, the remuneration of staff and senior managers responsible for the validation function is not linked to the performance of tasks relating to credit risk control or to originating or renewing exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy has no remuneration requirement for validation staff or senior managers.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that no undue influence is exercised on the conclusions, findings and recommendations of the validation function, where there is no separate validation unit.
rows.rationale: No requirement prevents undue influence on validation conclusions, findings and recommendations.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure effective separation between the staff performing the validation function and the staff performing other tasks, where there is no separate validation unit.
rows.quote: Validation is performed by the Model Validation team.
rows.rationale: The policy has a distinct Model Validation team, so the case of no separate validation unit does not arise.

rows.obligation: The institution shall organise its validation function in a way that is adequate for the nature, size and scale of the institution and the complexity of the risks inherent in its business model.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: Staffing is sized to the model inventory, but the policy does not require the validation organisation to fit the nature, size, scale and risk complexity of the business, and the team sits inside development.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the credit risk control unit or units are separate and independent of the personnel and management functions responsible for originating or renewing exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address separation of the credit risk control unit from personnel and management responsible for originating or renewing exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall organise the credit risk control unit or units as distinct organisational structures within the institution.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address organising the credit risk control unit as a distinct organisational structure.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the staff and senior management responsible for the credit risk control unit or units are not responsible for originating or renewing exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy does not say that credit risk control staff and senior management are not responsible for originating or renewing exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that senior managers of the credit risk control unit or units and of units responsible for originating or renewing exposures report to different members of the management body or of the committee designated by it.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address reporting of credit risk control and origination senior managers to different members of the management body.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the remuneration of the staff and senior management responsible for the credit risk control unit or units is not linked to the performance of tasks relating to originating or renewing exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address remuneration of credit risk control staff relative to origination tasks.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall not be involved in any aspect of the operation of the rating systems that it reviews.
rows.rationale: The policy does not state that Internal Audit must not be involved in the operation of the rating systems it reviews.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall be independent from the personnel and management responsible for originating or renewing exposures and shall report directly to senior management.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require Internal Audit to be independent from origination staff or to report directly to senior management.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the remuneration of the staff and senior management responsible for the internal audit function is not linked to the performance of tasks relating to originating or renewing exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address remuneration of Internal Audit staff and management.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 19
rows.obligation: The institution should have appropriate organisational arrangements (separate units reporting to different or the same senior management member, or separate staff within the same unit) to ensure the internal validation function is effectively independent from model development (design, development, implementation and monitoring).
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development, with a dotted reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer for validation matters.
rows.rationale: Validation sits in the development department under the Head of Model Development, and only the personal rule on validating one's own models is in place, so the independence arrangement is weak.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 19
rows.obligation: The institution should choose its validation independence arrangement taking into account the nature, size and scale of the institution and the complexity of the risks inherent in its business model.
rows.rationale: The policy does not say the independence arrangement was chosen by reference to the Bank's nature, size, scale and risk complexity.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 20
rows.obligation: Large and complex institutions should implement the most robust independence option for the validation function.
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development
rows.rationale: The Bank has many IRB models across several portfolios, yet validation is not separated from development (the least robust option), where the guide expects the most robust option for large and complex institutions.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 21
rows.obligation: Where the institution has the validation and development units report to the same member of senior management (option (b)), it should fulfil the additional requirements in Article 10(3) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2022/439.
rows.quote: Validators do not validate models they have developed themselves.
rows.rationale: Validation and development report to the same senior manager, but only a partial safeguard exists, with no further Art. 10(3) requirements such as separate staff or protection of validators.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 22
rows.obligation: The institution shall, when using option (c) of paragraph 19 for its validation function, fulfil the additional requirements specified in Article 10(4) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2022/439.
rows.quote: Where a validator was previously involved in the development of a model, another validator is assigned.
rows.rationale: Validation is a team within the development department, as in option (c), and only a validator-reassignment rule is in place, not the Art. 10(4) effective separation requirements.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 23
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the staff of the validation function is separate from the staff involved in the model development process.
rows.quote: The team is part of the Model Development & Analytics department and reports to the Head of Model Development
rows.rationale: The validation team sits within the development department and reports to the Head of Model Development, so its staff are not separate from model development staff.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 24
rows.obligation: The institution shall provide the validation function with suitable resources and experienced, qualified personnel with appropriate quantitative and qualitative knowledge to conduct an effective independent challenge of the internal models and estimates and their performance.
rows.quote: The Model Validation team is staffed with sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise for the Bank's model inventory.
rows.rationale: The policy requires sufficient quantitative and credit risk expertise, but does not address suitable resources generally or the capacity for effective independent challenge.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 30
rows.obligation: The institution shall dedicate sufficient time to the independent assessment by internal control functions for identifying and evaluating deficiencies in the rating system.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require dedicating sufficient time to the independent assessment by internal control functions to identify and evaluate rating system deficiencies.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 41
rows.obligation: The institution should clearly determine which individuals and/or teams make up the credit risk control function and which personnel and/or units are responsible for originating and renewing exposures, and why they are independent from one another.
rows.rationale: The policy does not identify the credit risk control function's composition or explain its independence from the units that originate and renew exposures.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 41
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure a direct line of reporting of the CRCU to senior management.
rows.rationale: The policy does not provide for a direct reporting line of the credit risk control unit to senior management.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform all analyses and tests so that it is in a position to propose an effective and independent challenge to model development and use.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Validation covers the main analyses, but it excludes external data and benchmarks and is not explicitly framed as performing all tests needed for effective independent challenge.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that the validation function has its own access to the relevant databases.
rows.rationale: The policy does not state that the validation function has its own access to the relevant databases.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform its analyses without considering input from the credit risk control unit, unless otherwise specified.
rows.rationale: The policy does not say that validation performs its analyses without considering input from the credit risk control unit.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: Internal audit should include in its general risk assessment its opinion on the validation function, in particular its independence from the CRCU and the scope and suitability of its tasks and outputs.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: Internal Audit reviews the validation function's independence, methods and report quality, but the policy does not mention independence from the CRCU, the scope and suitability of its tasks, or inclusion in the general risk assessment.

rows.obligation: The institution shall collect and store all relevant data to provide effective support to its credit risk measurement and management process.
rows.rationale: Collecting and storing all relevant data is a data management duty, not a validation duty; the policy only requires validation to check data quality.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have in place a process for vetting data inputs into the model.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness, and reviews the results of the data quality controls performed by the model owners.
rows.rationale: Validation reviews data quality controls, but the policy does not require a process for vetting data inputs into the model itself.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the data-vetting process an assessment of the accuracy, completeness and appropriateness of the data.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness
rows.rationale: Accuracy and completeness are covered but appropriateness of the data is not mentioned (timeliness is substituted).

rows.obligation: The model owner shall ensure the data used to build the model are representative of the population of the institution's actual obligors or exposures.
rows.rationale: No clause requires data to be representative of the actual obligor population; §6.2 even excludes external data and does not address representativeness.

rows.obligation: The institution shall consider a default to have occurred when it considers the obligor unlikely to pay its credit obligations to the institution, parent undertaking or subsidiaries in full without recourse to actions such as realising security.
rows.quote: the Bank considers the obligor unlikely to pay its credit obligations in full without realisation of collateral
rows.rationale: The unlikeliness-to-pay trigger is stated but omits obligations to the parent undertaking or subsidiaries.

rows.obligation: The institution shall consider a default to have occurred when the obligor is more than 90 days past due on any material credit obligation to the institution, the parent undertaking or any of its subsidiaries.
rows.quote: the obligor is more than 90 days past due on a material credit obligation
rows.rationale: The 90 days past due trigger is present but does not extend to obligations to the parent or subsidiaries.

rows.obligation: The institution shall start counting days past due for overdrafts once the obligor has breached an advised limit, been advised a limit smaller than current outstandings, or drawn credit without authorisation and the underlying amount is material.
rows.rationale: No rule on counting days past due for overdrafts.

rows.obligation: The institution shall start counting days past due for credit cards on the minimum payment due date.
rows.rationale: No rule on counting days past due for credit cards from the minimum payment due date.

rows.obligation: The institution shall assess materiality of a past due credit obligation against the threshold defined by the competent authority.
rows.quote: For retail exposures a credit obligation past due is material when the amount past due exceeds both EUR 100 and 1 % of the total on-balance-sheet exposure to that obligor. For other exposures the thresholds are EUR 500 and 1 %.
rows.rationale: The policy sets its own thresholds instead of using those defined by the competent authority, and non-retail EUR 500 is inconsistent with the regulatory threshold.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply its days-past-due counting policies consistently over time.
rows.rationale: No requirement of consistent application over time of days-past-due counting policies.

rows.obligation: The institution shall keep its days-past-due counting policies in line with its internal risk management and decision processes.
rows.rationale: Nothing on aligning days-past-due counting policies with internal risk management and decision processes.

rows.obligation: The institution shall treat the listed elements (non-accrued status, specific credit adjustment from significant perceived credit quality decline, sale at material credit-related economic loss, forbearance likely to diminish the financial obligation, bankruptcy filings by the institution or obligor) as indications of unlikeliness to pay.
rows.rationale: The default definition does not list non-accrued status, specific credit adjustments, distressed sales, forbearance or bankruptcy as unlikeliness-to-pay indications.

rows.obligation: The institution shall make appropriate adjustments to achieve broad equivalence with the definition of default when using external data that is not itself consistent with that definition.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used
rows.rationale: The policy excludes external data entirely, so no adjustments for default-definition equivalence are addressed; §7.5 only covers internal consistency.

rows.obligation: The institution shall rate the obligor or facility as a non-defaulted exposure when it considers that no default trigger continues to apply to a previously defaulted exposure.
rows.quote: An exposure returns to non-defaulted status when no default trigger has applied for one month and the obligor's situation has improved.
rows.rationale: Return to non-default when no trigger applies is stated, but with additional conditions and a one-month probation, and no explicit rating as non-defaulted.

rows.obligation: The institution shall deem another default to have occurred where the definition of default is subsequently triggered after a return to non-defaulted status.
rows.rationale: No clause states that a new trigger after return to non-default constitutes another default.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its own estimates of PD, LGD, conversion factor and EL incorporate all relevant data, information and methods.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Validation covers design and data generally, but nothing requires checking that estimates incorporate all relevant data, information and methods, and §6.2 excludes external sources.

rows.obligation: The institution shall derive its risk parameter estimates using both historical experience and empirical evidence, and not purely on judgemental considerations.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years
rows.rationale: Back-testing against historical experience is required, but validation of empirical evidence versus judgement in estimates is not explicitly required.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its risk parameter estimates are plausible and intuitive and based on the material drivers of the respective risk parameters.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to check plausibility, intuitiveness or that estimates are based on material risk drivers.

rows.obligation: The institution shall be able to provide a breakdown of its loss experience in terms of default frequency, LGD, conversion factor, or loss where EL estimates are used, by the factors it sees as the drivers of the respective risk parameters.
rows.rationale: No requirement for a breakdown of loss experience by drivers of the risk parameters.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its estimates are representative of long run experience.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: Long-run representativeness is checked for PD only, not for LGD, CCF or EL estimates.

rows.obligation: The institution shall take into account any changes in lending practice or the process for pursuing recoveries over the observation periods referred to in Article 180(1)(h) and (2)(e), Article 181(1)(j) and (2), and Article 182(2) and (3).
rows.quote: Validation reviews the treatment of incomplete recovery processes and of costs.
rows.rationale: Recovery-related treatment is reviewed for LGD, but changes in lending practice or recovery processes over observation periods are not addressed.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its estimates reflect the implications of technical advances and new data and other information as it becomes available.
rows.rationale: Nothing requires estimates to reflect technical advances and new data or information; §6.2 even excludes external data and benchmarks.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the population of exposures in the estimation data, the lending standards used when the data was generated and other relevant characteristics are comparable with those of its exposures and standards.
rows.rationale: No requirement to check comparability of the estimation data population, lending standards and characteristics with current exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the economic or market conditions underlying the estimation data are relevant to current and foreseeable conditions.
rows.rationale: No requirement to check that economic or market conditions in the data are relevant to current and foreseeable conditions.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the number of exposures in the sample and the data period used for quantification are sufficient to give confidence in the accuracy and robustness of its estimates.
rows.rationale: No requirement to check sample size or data period sufficiency for accuracy and robustness.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure estimates for purchased receivables reflect all relevant information available to it regarding the quality of the underlying receivables, including data for similar pools from the seller, itself or external sources.
rows.rationale: The policy's scope shows only retail and corporate exposures with no purchased receivables.

rows.obligation: The institution shall evaluate any data relied upon that is provided by the seller of purchased receivables.
rows.rationale: No purchased receivables are shown in the policy, so seller data evaluation does not apply.

rows.obligation: The institution using pooled data shall ensure the rating systems and criteria of other institutions in the pool are similar to its own.
rows.rationale: The policy shows no use of pooled data; validation relies on the Bank's internal data only.

rows.obligation: The institution using pooled data shall ensure the pool is representative of the portfolio for which the pooled data is used.
rows.rationale: The policy shows no use of pooled data; validation relies on the Bank's internal data only.

rows.obligation: The institution using pooled data shall use the pooled data consistently over time for its estimates.
rows.rationale: The policy shows no use of pooled data; validation relies on the Bank's internal data only.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its mapping analysis a comparison of the default definitions used, subject to the requirements in Article 178.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: The policy checks consistency of the default definition internally but does not require a mapping analysis comparing the default definitions of the data sources to Article 178.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use a historical observation period of at least five years for at least one source for PD estimation, whether external, internal or pooled data are used.
rows.rationale: No requirement on a minimum five-year historical observation period for PD estimation is stated.

rows.obligation: The institution shall regard internal data for assigning exposures to grades or pools as the primary source of information for estimating retail loss characteristics.
rows.rationale: The policy does not state that internal data is the primary source for estimating retail loss characteristics; it only says validation relies on internal data in a different context.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use external data or statistical models for retail quantification only where strong links exist between its grade assignment process and the external source's process, and between its internal risk profile and the composition of the external data.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: The policy has no condition on strong links for external data use; it excludes external data and benchmarks from validation altogether, which is inconsistent with the framework allowing their use under conditions.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use a historical observation period of at least five years for at least one source for retail PD estimation, whether external, internal or pooled data are used.
rows.rationale: No five-year minimum observation period for retail PD estimation is required.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use all relevant data sources as points of comparison for purchased retail receivables.
rows.rationale: The policy does not show the bank holds purchased retail receivables.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use a longer observation period where the available observation spans a longer period for any source and the data are relevant.
rows.rationale: No requirement to use a longer observation period where available and relevant.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the data used for retail PD estimation include a representative mix of good and bad years of the economic cycle relevant for the type of exposures.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: Long-run average review relates to cyclical representativeness but does not explicitly require a representative mix of good and bad years.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use a longer observation period where the available observation period spans a longer period for any source and the data are relevant.
rows.rationale: No requirement to use a longer observation period where available and relevant.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the data used for PD estimation include a representative mix of good and bad years of the economic cycle relevant for the type of exposures.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: Long-run average review relates to cyclical representativeness but does not explicitly require a representative mix of good and bad years.

rows.obligation: For corporate, institution, central government/central bank and regional government, local authority and public sector entity exposures, the institution shall base LGD estimates on data over a minimum of five years, increasing by one year each year after implementation until a minimum of seven years is reached, for at least one data source.
rows.quote: The Bank uses own estimates of PD, LGD and CCF for retail exposures and own estimates of PD for corporate exposures.
rows.rationale: The bank uses own LGD only for retail, so the corporate LGD period does not currently apply.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use the longer observation period for LGD estimates where the available observation period of any source spans a longer period and the data are relevant.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the longer LGD observation period where available and relevant.

rows.obligation: For retail exposures, the institution shall base LGD estimates on data over a minimum of five years.
rows.rationale: The policy has LGD sections but requires no minimum five-year data period for retail LGD estimates.

rows.obligation: The institution shall make use of historical data covering as long a period as possible in its comparisons of realised and estimated values.
rows.rationale: Back-testing is described without requiring use of historical data covering as long a period as possible.
