rows.obligation: The institution shall base its validation analysis on data that are appropriate to the portfolio, are updated regularly, and cover a relevant observation period.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness
rows.rationale: Data quality is checked, but appropriateness to the portfolio and relevance of the observation period are not required.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 71
rows.obligation: The institution shall consider that no default trigger continues to apply to a previously defaulted exposure only where at least 3 months have passed since the conditions in Articles 178(1)(b) and 178(3) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 ceased to be met.
rows.quote: An exposure returns to non-defaulted status when no default trigger has applied for one month and the obligor's situation has improved.
rows.rationale: The policy sets a one-month probation period, shorter than the required minimum of 3 months.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 71
rows.obligation: The institution shall take into account the behaviour of the obligor during the probation period when reclassifying a defaulted exposure to non-defaulted status.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the obligor's behaviour during a probation period to be considered when reclassifying to non-defaulted status.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 71
rows.obligation: The institution shall take into account the financial situation of the obligor during the probation period when reclassifying a defaulted exposure to non-defaulted status.
rows.quote: no default trigger has applied for one month and the obligor's situation has improved
rows.rationale: The policy requires that the obligor's situation has improved, but does not tie the financial situation assessment to the probation period.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 71
rows.obligation: The institution shall, after the probation period, assess the obligor and continue to classify exposures as defaulted where the obligor is still unlikely to pay in full without recourse to realising security, until the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent.
rows.rationale: The policy has no post-probation assessment requiring exposures to stay in default until the improvement is factual and permanent.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 71
rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the return-to-non-default conditions in points (a) to (d) also to new exposures to the obligor, in particular where previous defaulted exposures were sold or written off.
rows.rationale: The policy does not extend return-to-non-default conditions to new exposures of the obligor, including where previous defaulted exposures were sold or written off.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 72
rows.obligation: The institution shall consider that no default trigger continues to apply to a defaulted exposure subject to distressed restructuring only where at least 1 year has passed from the latest of the extension of restructuring measures, the classification as defaulted, or the end of the grace period.
rows.quote: Exposures subject to distressed restructuring remain in default for at least one year.
rows.rationale: The one-year minimum is stated, but the policy does not define the starting point as the latest of the restructuring extension, default classification or end of grace period.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 73
rows.obligation: The institution shall reclassify a distressed-restructured exposure to non-defaulted status after at least one year only where all listed conditions are met (material payment made, regular payments per schedule, no past-due obligations, no unlikeliness-to-pay indications, no other expectation of non-payment in full without realising security).
rows.rationale: The policy lists none of the cumulative conditions (material payment, regular payments, no past-due amounts, no UTP indications) for reclassifying restructured exposures.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 73
rows.obligation: The institution shall examine in particular situations where a large lump-sum payment or significantly larger payments are envisaged at the end of the repayment schedule when assessing whether the obligor is unlikely to pay.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address examining large lump-sum or significantly larger final payments in the repayment schedule.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 73
rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the return-to-non-default conditions in points (a) to (e) also to new exposures to the obligor, in particular where previous defaulted exposures subject to distressed restructuring were sold or written off.
rows.rationale: The policy does not apply the return-to-non-default conditions for restructured exposures to new exposures of the obligor.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 74
rows.obligation: The institution shall not apply the material payment condition of paragraph 73(a) where the obligor changes due to a merger, acquisition or similar transaction.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the material payment condition or the treatment of a change of obligor through merger or acquisition.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 74
rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the material payment condition of paragraph 73(a) where only the obligor's name changes.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the material payment condition or the treatment of a change of obligor name only.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 75
rows.obligation: The institution shall define clear criteria and policies for when an obligor can be classified back to non-defaulted status, including when the improvement in financial situation is sufficient for full and timely repayment.
rows.quote: An exposure returns to non-defaulted status when no default trigger has applied for one month and the obligor's situation has improved.
rows.rationale: The policy gives a return criterion, but it is vague and does not define when the improvement is sufficient for full and timely repayment.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 75
rows.obligation: The institution shall define criteria for when repayment is actually likely to be made even where the obligor's financial situation has improved.
rows.rationale: The policy defines no criteria for when repayment is actually likely despite an improved financial situation.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 76
rows.obligation: The institution shall regularly monitor the effectiveness of its return-to-non-default policies.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no requirement to monitor the effectiveness of return-to-non-default policies; §7.5 covers only consistency of the default definition.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 76
rows.obligation: The institution shall monitor and analyse changes of status of obligors or facilities.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require monitoring or analysis of changes of status of obligors or facilities.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 76
rows.obligation: The institution shall monitor and analyse the impact of its return-to-non-default policies on cure rates.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to monitor or analyse the impact of return-to-non-default policies on cure rates; §7.4 only sets the return rule.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 76
rows.obligation: The institution shall monitor and analyse the impact of its return-to-non-default policies on multiple defaults.
rows.rationale: No monitoring or analysis of the impact of return-to-non-default policies on multiple defaults is required.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 77
rows.obligation: The institution shall revise its policies on reclassification of exposures in the case of an extensive number of multiple defaults.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to revise reclassification policies when there are many multiple defaults.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 78
rows.obligation: The institution shall take the analysis of changes in obligor or facility statuses into account when specifying the probation periods referred to in paragraphs 71 and 72.
rows.rationale: No link between analysis of status changes and the specification of probation periods is stated.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 79
rows.obligation: The institution shall adopt adequate mechanisms and procedures to ensure the definition of default is implemented and used correctly.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Validation checks consistent application, but there are no mechanisms or procedures to ensure the definition is implemented and used correctly.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 79
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that default of a single obligor is identified consistently across the institution for all exposures, in all relevant IT systems, legal entities within the group and geographical locations.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Consistency is checked across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, but obligor-level identification across all IT systems and geographical locations is not addressed.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 79
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that either the same definition of default is used consistently across the institution, parent and subsidiaries and types of exposures, or the scope of application of each differing definition is clearly specified.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: The policy requires a consistent single definition across portfolios and subsidiaries and validation checks it.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 80
rows.obligation: The institution shall implement adequate procedures and mechanisms to ensure default of a single obligor is identified consistently across all exposures, IT systems, group legal entities and geographical locations.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Only a validation check of consistency exists; there are no implementation procedures or mechanisms for single-obligor identification across IT systems and locations.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 81
rows.obligation: The institution using the IRB Approach shall estimate the materiality of inconsistencies in default identification caused by legal data-sharing impediments and their possible impact on risk parameter estimates.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address legal data-sharing impediments or estimating the materiality of resulting inconsistencies.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 82
rows.obligation: The institution shall demonstrate that the effect of non-compliance is immaterial (no or very few common clients among group entities and immaterial exposure to them) if it does not apply mechanisms for fully consistent default identification across the group.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no demonstration of immateriality where group-wide consistent default identification is not applied.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 83
rows.obligation: The institution should use the same definition of default for a single type of exposures as defined in point (2) of Article 142(1) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, across the institution, its parent undertaking and subsidiaries.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: A single default definition is set in §7.2 and its consistent use across portfolios and subsidiaries is checked.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 84
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that its internal procedures clearly specify the scope of application of each definition of default where different definitions are applied.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: The policy applies a single definition of default throughout, so specifying the scope of differing definitions does not arise.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 84
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that the definition of default specified for a certain type of exposures, legal entity or geographical location is applied consistently to all exposures within the scope of that definition.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Validation checks that the definition is applied consistently to all models, portfolios and subsidiaries.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 85
rows.obligation: The institution using the IRB Approach shall adequately reflect the use of different default definitions in the estimation of risk parameters for rating systems whose scope encompasses different default definitions.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: The policy uses one default definition, so reflecting different definitions in parameter estimation does not apply.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 106
rows.obligation: The institution should have effective processes to obtain relevant information to identify defaults in a timely manner and channel it in the shortest possible time, where possible automatically, to the personnel responsible for credit decisions.
rows.rationale: Processes for obtaining default information and channelling it to credit decision personnel are operational and belong in a rating-system operation or data management document, not a validation policy.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 106
rows.obligation: The institution should perform identification of indications of default on a daily basis where it applies automatic processes such as counting of days past due.
rows.rationale: Daily operational default identification (counting days past due) is a rating-system operation/credit process duty, not a validation policy matter; §7 only defines default and validation checks.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 106
rows.obligation: The institution should update information used in manual default identification processes with a frequency that guarantees timely identification of default.
rows.rationale: Update frequency of information in manual default identification is an operational process duty belonging in default management procedures.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 107
rows.obligation: The institution should verify on a regular basis that all forborne non-performing exposures are classified as default and subject to distressed restructuring.
rows.rationale: The policy has a default section but nothing requires validation to verify that forborne non-performing exposures are classified as default and distressed restructuring.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 107
rows.obligation: The institution should analyse on a regular basis forborne performing exposures to determine whether any fulfils the indication of unlikeliness to pay under Article 178(3)(d) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and paragraphs 49 to 55.
rows.rationale: No requirement to analyse forborne performing exposures for unlikeliness to pay indications under Article 178(3)(d).

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 108
rows.obligation: The institution should have control mechanisms ensuring that relevant information is used in the default identification process immediately after being obtained.
rows.rationale: Control mechanisms for immediate use of information in default identification are operational controls, not validation policy content.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 108
rows.obligation: The institution should mark all exposures to a defaulted obligor (or all relevant exposures where default is applied at facility level for retail) as defaulted in all relevant IT systems without undue delay.
rows.rationale: Marking defaulted exposures across IT systems is an operational/IT process duty outside the validation policy.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 108
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that delays in recording default do not lead to errors or inconsistencies in risk management, risk reporting, own funds requirements calculation or the use of data in risk quantification.
rows.rationale: Preventing errors from delayed default recording is an operational data/process duty, not a validation obligation.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the same definition of default for the same historical observations used in different models within a rating system when quantifying risk parameters.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Validation must check consistent default definition across models and in estimation data, matching the requirement.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the same treatment of multiple defaults of the same obligor or exposure across internal, external and pooled data sources.
rows.rationale: Nothing addresses consistent treatment of multiple defaults across internal, external and pooled data; §9.3 covers only repeated defaults in realised LGD data, and external data is excluded.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that its data quality policies apply to all data used in model development and calibration.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness, and reviews the results of the data quality controls performed by the model owners.
rows.rationale: Validation checks data used for estimation, but there is no data quality policy requirement applying to all development and calibration data.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that its data quality policies apply to the data used in the application of the risk parameters.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness, and reviews the results of the data quality controls performed by the model owners.
rows.rationale: Application data is checked for completeness, accuracy and timeliness, but there is no requirement that data quality policies apply to it.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that data used in model development and as model inputs is sufficiently precise to avoid material distortions of the outcome of the assignment of exposures to grades or pools.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness
rows.rationale: Accuracy is checked but not sufficient precision to avoid material distortion of grade/pool assignment.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that data used in model development and application does not contain biases that make the data unfit for purpose.
rows.rationale: No requirement that validation check data for biases that make it unfit for purpose.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have sound policies, processes and methods for assessing the representativeness of data used for the estimation of risk parameters.
rows.rationale: The policy has no policies, processes or methods for assessing data representativeness; §6.2 even dismisses external data as not representative without assessment.

rows.obligation: The institution shall specify in its internal policies the statistical tests and metrics used to assess representativeness of data used for risk differentiation and, separately, of data underlying risk quantification.
rows.rationale: No statistical tests or metrics for data representativeness are specified, for risk differentiation or risk quantification; the Annex covers only performance tests.

rows.obligation: The institution shall specify methods for qualitative assessment of data representativeness for cases defined in its policies where statistical tests cannot be applied.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for qualitative assessment methods of data representativeness where statistical tests cannot be applied.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use the same standards and methods to assess representativeness of data from different sources (internal, external, pooled), unless different methods are justified by the specificity of the data source or availability of information.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: The policy excludes external data and so sets no common representativeness standard across internal, external and pooled sources, and it presumes external data is unrepresentative without assessing it.

rows.obligation: The institution shall obtain sufficient information from data providers to assess the representativeness of external or pooled data to its own portfolios and processes.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to obtain information from data providers on external or pooled data representativeness, and §6.2 rules out external data.

rows.obligation: The institution shall analyse the representativeness of data for statistical models and other mechanical methods used to assign exposures to grades or pools, and for statistical default prediction models.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness
rows.rationale: Data checks cover completeness, accuracy and timeliness but not representativeness analysis for rating assignment or default prediction models.

rows.obligation: The institution shall select an appropriate model development dataset so that model performance on the application portfolio, in particular discriminatory power, is not significantly hindered by insufficient data representativeness.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address selecting a development dataset so that representativeness does not hinder performance.

rows.obligation: The institution shall analyse, at the model development stage, the representativeness of the data in terms of scope of application, definition of default, distribution of relevant risk characteristics, and lending standards and recovery policies.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Only the definition of default consistency is checked, with no representativeness analysis of scope of application, risk characteristic distributions, lending standards or recovery policies.

rows.obligation: The institution shall analyse the segmentation of exposures and consider whether the scope of application of the model changed over the period covered by the development data.
rows.rationale: The policy has no analysis of segmentation or of changes in model scope over the development data period.

rows.obligation: The institution shall, where the model scope changed, analyse the relevant risk drivers by comparing their distribution in the RDS before and after the change and with the application portfolio.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require comparing risk driver distributions in the RDS before and after a scope change or with the application portfolio.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply statistical methodologies such as cluster analysis or similar techniques to demonstrate representativeness when the model scope changed.
rows.rationale: The policy mentions no cluster analysis or similar statistical techniques to demonstrate representativeness after scope changes.

rows.obligation: The institution shall, for pooled models, perform the scope representativeness analysis with regard to the part of the model scope that it uses.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address pooled models or scope representativeness for the part of the scope used.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the definition of default underlying model development data is consistent over time.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Validation checks consistent application of the default definition in estimation data, which broadly matches the consistency requirement, though over-time consistency is not explicit.

rows.obligation: The institution shall make adjustments to achieve consistency with the current default definition where the default definition changed during the observation period.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require adjusting historical data for changes in the default definition during the observation period.

rows.obligation: The institution shall adopt adequate measures where the model covers exposures in several jurisdictions having or having had different default definitions.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Consistency across subsidiaries is checked, but no measures are required for jurisdictions with different current or past default definitions.

rows.obligation: The institution shall analyse the definition of default in each data source separately.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require analysing the default definition in each data source separately.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that a model-development default definition differing from the Article 178 definition does not negatively impact the rating model's risk differentiation and predictive power.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the impact on risk differentiation and predictive power of a development default definition differing from Article 178.

rows.obligation: The institution shall analyse the distribution and range of values of key risk characteristics of the development data used for risk differentiation in comparison with the application portfolio.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to compare the distribution and range of key risk characteristics in the development data with the application portfolio.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse the representativeness of the data in terms of portfolio structure by relevant risk characteristics, using statistical tests specified in its policies, to ensure the range of values observed in the application portfolio is adequately reflected in the development sample.
rows.rationale: No requirement to analyse representativeness of development data by portfolio structure using statistical tests.

rows.obligation: Where statistical tests cannot be applied, the institution should carry out at least a qualitative analysis based on descriptive statistics of the portfolio structure, taking into account possible seasoning effects under Article 180(2)(f) CRR.
rows.rationale: No qualitative representativeness analysis or consideration of seasoning effects is required.

rows.obligation: The institution should take into account the sensitivity of the risk characteristics to economic conditions when considering the results of the representativeness analysis.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention the sensitivity of risk characteristics to economic conditions in a representativeness analysis.

rows.obligation: The institution should address material differences in key risk characteristics between the data sample and the application portfolio, for example by using another data sample or a subset of observations or by reflecting these characteristics as risk drivers in the model.
rows.rationale: No requirement to address material differences between data sample and application portfolio, such as using another sample or adding risk drivers.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse whether, over the relevant historical observation period, there were significant changes in lending standards, recovery policies or the legal environment that may influence the level of risk or the distribution of risk characteristics in the portfolio covered by the model.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require analysis of changes in lending standards, recovery policies or legal environment over the observation period.

rows.obligation: Where the institution observes such changes in lending standards, recovery policies or legal environment, it should compare the data included in the RDS before and after the change of policy.
rows.rationale: No requirement to compare RDS data before and after a policy change.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure comparability of current underwriting or recovery standards with those applied to the observations included in the RDS and used for model development.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address comparability of current underwriting or recovery standards with those in the RDS.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse the comparability of data used to calculate long-run average default rates or long-run average LGDs, and where relevant the representativeness of the pool, in terms of scope of application, definition of default, distribution of risk characteristics, current and foreseeable economic or market conditions, and lending standards and recovery policies.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: The policy reviews the long-run average nature of PD but does not require analysing comparability of the data in terms of scope, default definition, risk characteristics, economic conditions and lending or recovery policies.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse the scope of application of the calibration data as specified in paragraph 22.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require analysis of the scope of application of the calibration data.

rows.obligation: The institution should compare the definition of default it currently applies with the definitions used for the observations in the dataset used for risk quantification, to ensure consistency with Article 178 CRR.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Consistency of the default definition in estimation data is checked, but not explicitly against Article 178 CRR or historical data definitions; the policy's own definition (e.g. one-month return to non-default) is also not aligned with the CRR.

rows.obligation: Where the definition of default changed during the historical observation period, the institution should assess the representativeness of historical data in the RDS used for risk quantification in the same way as for external data under Chapter 6 of the EBA Guidelines on the definition of default.
rows.rationale: No treatment of changes in the definition of default during the observation period or representativeness assessment of historical data.

rows.obligation: Where the definition of default changed more than once during the historical observation period, the institution should analyse each past definition of default separately.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require separate analysis of each past definition of default where it changed more than once.

rows.obligation: The institution should perform an appropriate analysis to ensure that, at calibration segment level, the ranges of values of key risk characteristics in the application portfolio are comparable to those in the reference data set to the degree required to ensure unbiased risk quantification.
rows.rationale: No analysis at calibration segment level of comparability of key risk characteristic ranges between the application portfolio and the reference data set.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse whether there were significant changes in lending standards or recovery policies over the historical observation period that may influence the level of risk or the distribution of risk driver characteristics in the portfolio covered by the model.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require analysis of changes in lending standards or recovery policies over the historical observation period.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the annual review an analysis of data representativeness, covering differences between the RDS used to quantify the risk parameter and the application portfolio, including portfolio changes and structural breaks.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to analyse representativeness of the RDS versus the application portfolio, including portfolio changes and structural breaks.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the annual review an analysis of differences between the RDS used to develop the model and the application portfolio, performing the analyses in paragraphs 24, 25 and 26, and those in paragraphs 22 and 23 where model performance is deteriorating.
rows.rationale: No analysis of differences between the development data and the application portfolio (paras 22-26) is required in the annual validation.

rows.obligation: The institution should apply consistent policies for data adjustments and exclusions for the purpose of the review in paragraphs 217 to 220.
rows.rationale: The policy has no provision on consistent policies for data adjustments and exclusions in the review.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that any differences in the policies applied to the relevant datasets are justified and do not distort the results of the review.
rows.rationale: Nothing requires justification of differences in data adjustment or exclusion policies across datasets.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the relevant loss data is available during the considered downturn period as well as during an appropriate period before and after it.
rows.rationale: The LGD validation section does not address availability of loss data during downturn periods and the periods before and after them.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that, for rating systems developed from pooled data, the validation function has access to all relevant internal data of that institution.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address validation access to internal data for pooled-data rating systems.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should use complementary analyses for exposure types where quantitative measures are inconclusive because data are scarce.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used
rows.rationale: The policy excludes external benchmarks and complementary analyses, which conflicts with using complementary analyses where quantitative measures are inconclusive.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should consider adjusting its internal data following significant changes applied to an external credit bureau score used as a main driver of the internal rating, and whenever the input variables are no longer appropriate.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address changes to an external credit bureau score used as a rating driver or adjusting internal data accordingly.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should analyse individual defaults (or at least a sample where analysing all is unduly burdensome) when the number of defaults is low, to check that the main drivers of observed defaults are appropriately reflected in the model.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to analyse individual defaults when defaults are few.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the data used to build the model are representative of the actual obligors or exposures.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness
rows.rationale: Data quality is checked, but representativeness of the model-building data for actual obligors or exposures is not required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should monitor changes made to the definition of default to identify any that would affect the representativeness of the dataset for obligors or facilities within the model's range of application.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Consistency of the default definition is checked, but changes to it and their effect on dataset representativeness are not monitored.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should analyse lending standards or workout procedures, external market and economic conditions, and other relevant characteristics surrounding the model development process.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to analyse lending standards, workout procedures, market and economic conditions around model development.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should, where it uses data pooled across institutions, also cover the requirements of Article 179(2) paragraphs (a) and (b) of the CRR in its representativeness analyses.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address pooled data across institutions or the Article 179(2) requirements.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should evaluate input data to ensure the data treatment process is reliable and well-founded.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness, and reviews the results of the data quality controls performed by the model owners.
rows.rationale: Data quality is checked, but the reliability and soundness of the data treatment process is not explicitly evaluated.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should ensure that necessary information is available and up to date for the majority of the application portfolio's obligors and facilities by tracking the age of model input data, especially financial statements.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness
rows.rationale: Timeliness is checked generally, but there is no explicit tracking of the age of input data such as financial statements across the application portfolio.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should ensure that all defaults within the model's scope of application are correctly identified and fully documented and registered in the appropriate and intended IT systems.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Validation checks consistent application of the default definition and data completeness/accuracy, but does not require checking that all defaults are correctly identified, documented and registered in the intended IT systems.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should ensure that the number and reasons for technical past-due situations are tracked.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no requirement for validation to track the number and reasons for technical past-due situations.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform data cleansing analyses, covering the exclusion of observations and the reasons for them from the risk database used to construct the reference dataset, at least at initial validation.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to perform data cleansing analyses on exclusions of observations and their reasons from the risk database, at initial validation or otherwise; §7.1 only covers completeness, accuracy and timeliness.

rows.obligation: The institution shall document its rating systems and the rationale for their design.
rows.rationale: Documenting rating systems and design rationale is a model development/documentation duty, not a validation policy matter (§3.3 only assigns documentation to developers).

rows.obligation: The institution shall document how human judgement and model results are to be combined.
rows.rationale: Documenting how human judgement and model results are combined is a model development/rating-system operation standard, and the policy has no section on overrides.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have documented policies on the counting of days past due, in particular re-ageing of facilities and the granting of extensions, amendments or deferrals, renewals, and netting of existing accounts.
rows.rationale: The policy has a default section (§7) but says nothing on counting days past due, re-ageing, extensions, deferrals, renewals or netting, and does not require validation to check them.

rows.obligation: The institution shall document, and ensure are reasonable, any differences between estimates used for calculating risk weights and those used for internal purposes.
rows.rationale: No clause addresses documenting or checking differences between regulatory estimates and internal-purpose estimates.

rows.obligation: The institution shall document the basis for the mapping of internal grades to the external scale.
rows.rationale: Mapping of internal grades to the external scale is a rating-system design/calibration matter, with no mapping section in this policy.

rows.obligation: The institution shall document the methods and data used in comparisons of realised and estimated values.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: Validation reports are required but there is no explicit requirement to document the methods and data used in realised-versus-estimated comparisons.

rows.obligation: The institution shall document changes in estimation and validation methods and data (both data sources and periods covered).
rows.rationale: No clause requires documenting changes in estimation and validation methods and data sources or periods.

rows.obligation: The institution shall document and retain changes to the rating process, criteria or individual rating parameters.
rows.quote: Changes are recorded in the version history held in the Bank's policy register.
rows.rationale: Only changes to this policy are recorded, and the inventory keeps limited data; there is no requirement to document and retain changes to the rating process, criteria or parameters.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 109
rows.obligation: The institution should document its policies on the definition of default, including all triggers for identification of default, the exit criteria and a clear identification of the scope of application.
rows.quote: An obligor is in default when (a) the Bank considers the obligor unlikely to pay its credit obligations in full without realisation of collateral, or (b) the obligor is more than 90 days past due on a material credit obligation.
rows.rationale: The policy states the default definition with triggers and exit criteria but does not require documenting all triggers, the exit criteria and the scope of application as a documented policy.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 109
rows.obligation: The institution should document the operationalisation of all indications of default.
rows.rationale: Nothing requires documenting the operationalisation of the indications of default (the unlikeliness-to-pay indicators are not elaborated).

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 109
rows.obligation: The institution should document the operationalisation of the criteria for reclassification of a defaulted obligor to a non-defaulted status.
rows.quote: An exposure returns to non-defaulted status when no default trigger has applied for one month and the obligor's situation has improved.
rows.rationale: Return criteria are stated but there is no requirement to document their operationalisation (and the one-month period is vague).

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 109
rows.obligation: The institution should keep an updated register of all definitions of default.
rows.rationale: No register of definitions of default is required; §7.5 only checks consistent application.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 110
rows.obligation: The institution should document the application of the definition of default in detail, including the process, sources of information and responsibilities for identifying each indication of default.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to document the process, information sources and responsibilities for identifying each default indication.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 111
rows.obligation: The institution should document the criteria for reclassification of a defaulted obligor to non-defaulted status, including processes, sources of information and responsibilities assigned to relevant personnel.
rows.rationale: §7.4 gives return criteria but no documentation of processes, sources of information and responsibilities for reclassification.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 112
rows.obligation: The institution should include in its default documentation a description of all automatic mechanisms and manual processes.
rows.rationale: No requirement to describe automatic mechanisms and manual processes in default documentation.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 112
rows.obligation: The institution should describe manually applied qualitative indications of default or return-to-non-default criteria in sufficient detail to facilitate common understanding and consistent application by all responsible personnel.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address describing manually applied qualitative default indicators or return-to-non-default criteria in detail for consistent application.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 113
rows.obligation: The institution should keep an updated register of all current and past versions of the default definition, at least starting from the date of application of the guidelines.
rows.rationale: No register of current and past versions of the default definition is required; the version history in §1.4 concerns the Policy itself.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 113
rows.obligation: The institution should record in the default definition register the scope of application, the approving body and approval date, implementation date, a brief description of changes versus the last version, and for IRB institutions the change category, date of submission to competent authorities and approval date.
rows.rationale: No default definition register content (scope, approving body, dates, change category) is specified.

rows.obligation: The institution should document the difference between the proportion of defaulted and non-defaulted exposures in the development dataset and in the application portfolio.
rows.rationale: Documenting differences in default proportions between development dataset and application portfolio is a model development documentation duty, and the policy's data section does not require validation to check it.

rows.obligation: The institution should document the application of human judgement in the model, including at least the criteria for the assessment, rationale, assumptions, experts involved and description of the process.
rows.rationale: Documentation of human judgement in the model is a model development documentation duty, not addressed by the validation policy.

rows.obligation: The institution should provide evidence that applying an appropriate adjustment results in a best estimate.
rows.rationale: The policy has a MoC section but nothing requires evidence that adjustments result in a best estimate; validation of such adjustments is not addressed.

rows.obligation: The institution should document the methods used to apply appropriate adjustments to rectify identified deficiencies, where relevant, and their justification.
rows.rationale: Methods and justification for adjustments rectifying deficiencies are not addressed, although the MoC section exists and validation should check them.

rows.obligation: The institution shall document the MoC applied for each rating system in the relevant model documentation and methodology manuals.
rows.quote: The overall MoC and its components are documented in the model documentation and in the validation report.
rows.rationale: The policy requires MoC documentation in the model documentation, matching the obligation.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the MoC documentation a complete list of all identified deficiencies, including errors and uncertainties, and the potentially affected model components or risk parameters.
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A)
rows.rationale: Deficiencies are reviewed and MoC documented, but no complete list of all deficiencies (including errors and uncertainties) and affected components is required.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the MoC documentation the category under which each identified deficiency is classified, as referred to in paragraph 42.
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A)
rows.rationale: Only Category A is mentioned; the classification of each deficiency by category is not required in the MoC documentation.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the MoC documentation a description of the methods for quantifying the MoC for identified deficiencies, in particular the methodologies used per category.
rows.rationale: No description of MoC quantification methods per category is required in documentation.

rows.obligation: The institution shall define the roles and responsibilities of all staff involved in the validation function and maintain validation manuals.
rows.quote: Validation is performed by the Model Validation team.
rows.rationale: The policy states some validation roles but defines no roles and responsibilities of all validation staff and no validation manuals are required.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall clearly specify in its validation methods and procedures the validation objectives, standards and limitations.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation methods and procedures to specify objectives, standards and limitations.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall describe in its validation methods and procedures all validation tests, data sets and data cleansing processes.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Some tests are listed, but there is no requirement to describe all tests, data sets and data cleansing processes in validation procedures.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall set out data sources and reference time periods in its validation methods and procedures.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used
rows.rationale: Data sources are only broadly stated and reference time periods are not set out in validation methods and procedures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall clearly lay down its decision-making process, hierarchy, reporting lines and levels of responsibility in its internal documentation.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: Section 3 lays down roles, approval hierarchy and reporting lines (e.g. §4.1 reporting line of validation, §3.4 approval of new/changed systems) for model governance.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its change policy procedures for the documentation of implemented changes to rating systems.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: Documentation procedures for implemented rating-system changes belong in a change policy, not in the validation policy, which only touches on change approval.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should maintain a written model risk management policy that includes a definition of what constitutes a model, the institution's interpretation of model risk, and a description of the model risk framework components (model governance, risk control function, validation function, internal audit) and their documented policies.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The policy describes governance, validation and internal audit roles but contains no definition of a model, no interpretation of model risk and no full model risk management framework description.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 14
rows.obligation: The institution should clearly describe the composition of the management body and the senior management in its internal documentation.
rows.rationale: Describing the composition of the management body and senior management belongs in general governance documents, not a validation policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 15
rows.obligation: The institution should document the roles and responsibilities of each individual in the management body.
rows.quote: The **Management Board** approves this Policy and receives the annual validation report.
rows.rationale: Individual roles of management body members belong in general governance charters; the policy only gives the Management Board's collective role in validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 16
rows.obligation: The institution should clearly document the composition, mandate and reporting lines of committees responsible for internal model governance and oversight, as well as the decisions taken.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The MRC's chair and mandate are described, but its composition and the documentation of its decisions are not specified.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 17
rows.obligation: The senior management should clearly document its decision-making procedures relating to all aspects of internal models.
rows.rationale: Senior management's decision-making procedures across all aspects of internal models belong in general governance documentation rather than a validation policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 27
rows.obligation: The institution shall document the approvals of material aspects of rating and estimation processes so they can be made available for review at the request of internal audit or the competent authority.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require documentation of approvals of material aspects of rating and estimation processes to be available for internal audit or the competent authority.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 29
rows.obligation: The institution shall clearly explain and document the use of expert judgement within the classification of material changes or exceptions.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address documenting the use of expert judgement in classifying material changes or exceptions.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should document the results of validation analyses and tests, including preparation of validation data, in a validation report verifiable by third-party experts such as internal audit and the competent authority.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: A report is required for every validation, but there is no requirement to document tests and validation data preparation so that third parties can verify them.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 53
rows.obligation: The institution should clearly justify and document deviations from the one-year yearly validation duration.
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: Annual validation is required but PD back-testing is done every two years, a deviation from the annual cycle with no justification or documentation requirement.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 65
rows.obligation: Internal audit should document the auditing techniques used to ensure that assessments are consistent.
rows.rationale: Internal audit review is described but there is no requirement to document the auditing techniques used to ensure consistent assessments.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 68
rows.obligation: The institution should clearly document the responsibilities of its different internal control functions with respect to the independent assessment (e.g. definition of default, IT implementation of the rating system, assignment of exposures to exposure classes).
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: Responsibilities of validation and internal audit are described, but not documented for the independent assessment of items such as default definition, IT implementation or exposure class assignment.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution shall document the situations in which human judgement may override the inputs or outputs of the grade and pool assignment process.
rows.rationale: Documenting situations where human judgement may override grade or pool assignment belongs in rating-system operation documents, not the validation policy, which has no section on overrides.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should check that the descriptions of the data sources, variables and risk drivers used for development are properly documented.
rows.quote: Validation checks the data used for estimation and application for completeness, accuracy and timeliness, and reviews the results of the data quality controls performed by the model owners.
rows.rationale: Validation checks data quality but not that descriptions of data sources, variables and risk drivers are properly documented.

rows.obligation: The institution shall validate its rating systems.
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: The policy requires regular validation of all rating systems in use.

rows.obligation: The institution shall validate each rating system during an appropriate period prior to the permission to use that rating system.
rows.quote: **Initial validation** is performed for every new rating system before the Bank applies for permission to use it or before its first use for own funds requirements.
rows.rationale: Initial validation is required before the permission application and before first use.

rows.obligation: The institution shall assess, during the pre-permission validation period, whether each rating system is suited to its range of application.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Initial validation is required, but the policy does not state that it assesses whether the system is suited to its range of application (the scope of application is only recorded in the inventory).

rows.obligation: The validation function shall run a regular cycle of model validation that includes monitoring of model performance and stability.
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use. It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability)
rows.rationale: A regular annual cycle covers performance and stability monitoring.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall include review of model specification in the regular cycle of model validation.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance
rows.rationale: Model design review is explicitly part of the regular validation.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall include testing of model outputs against outcomes in the regular cycle of model validation.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years
rows.rationale: Outcome testing is required, but PD back-testing is only biennial, which is less frequent than the annual regular cycle, so it is not fully consistent.

rows.obligation: The institution shall review its estimates when new information comes to light but at least on an annual basis.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Annual validation exists, but the policy does not explicitly require a review of estimates annually and when new information comes to light; updates are triggered only by material deficiencies.

rows.obligation: The institution shall validate its internal estimates in accordance with the requirements of Article 185.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used
rows.rationale: Validation of estimates is covered in detail, but the exclusion of external benchmarks and biennial PD back-testing fall short of Article 185.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have robust systems in place to validate the accuracy and consistency of rating systems, processes and the estimation of all relevant risk parameters.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: Validation covers accuracy and consistency of rating systems, processes and parameter estimates (PD, LGD, CCF) across sections 7-10.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its internal validation process enables it to assess the performance of internal rating and risk estimation systems consistently and meaningfully.
rows.quote: **Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Performance assessment is defined with standard tests, but the lack of external benchmarks and the inconsistent frequencies limit meaningful assessment.

rows.obligation: The institution shall update the comparison analysis and documentation at least annually.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years, using binomial and Jeffreys tests.
rows.rationale: PD comparison of realised and estimated values is done every two years, not at least annually as required.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use other quantitative validation tools and comparisons with relevant external data sources in addition to its core validation.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: The policy explicitly excludes the external data comparisons that the regulation requires.

rows.obligation: The institution shall base its internal assessments of the performance of its rating systems on as long a period as possible.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require performance assessments to be based on as long a period as possible.

rows.obligation: The institution shall keep the methods and data used for quantitative validation consistent through time.
rows.quote: **Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Standard tests and tolerances in the Annex give some consistency over time, but there is no explicit requirement to keep methods and data consistent through time.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall test and monitor grades and pools.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: Grades are tested and monitored by validation, but the policy does not address pools generally and the validation unit sits under the Head of Model Development, so it is not a separate credit risk control unit.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall implement procedures to verify that grade and pool definitions are consistently applied across departments and geographic areas.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Consistency checks are required only for the definition of default, not for grade and pool definitions across departments and geographic areas.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall review the rating criteria to evaluate if they remain predictive of risk.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: Grade assignment and the rating process are reviewed, but there is no explicit review of whether the rating criteria remain predictive of risk.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have a framework for regular reviews of estimates that includes a minimum scope and frequency of analyses, including predefined metrics to test data representativeness, model performance, predictive power and stability.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: The policy sets a scope and metrics for performance and stability, but defines no predefined metrics to test data representativeness.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its review framework predefined standards, including predefined thresholds and significance levels for the relevant metrics.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: The Annex defines thresholds and significance levels (AUC, Jeffreys p-values, PSI, LGD and CCF differences) for the standard tests.

rows.obligation: The institution shall perform reviews of estimates at least annually, taking into account the metrics, standards and thresholds it defined under paragraph 217.
rows.quote: Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: The annual review frequency is met and uses the predefined metrics and tolerance thresholds in the Annex.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the annual review an analysis of model performance and stability over time that identifies potential deterioration, including discriminatory power, by comparing development-time performance against each subsequent observation period and the predefined thresholds, on relevant subsets.
rows.quote: Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Discriminatory power is compared against the initial validation with thresholds, but there is no comparison against each subsequent observation period and no analysis on relevant subsets.

rows.obligation: The institution shall perform the model performance analysis on the whole application portfolio without data adjustments or exclusions made in model development, and obtain development-time performance for the whole application portfolio prior to any adjustments or exclusions.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require performance analysis on the whole application portfolio without development-time adjustments or exclusions.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the annual review a back-testing analysis comparing the estimates used for own funds requirements against observed outcomes for each grade or pool.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years, using binomial and Jeffreys tests.
rows.rationale: PD back-testing is only every two years, below the annual requirement, though LGD and CCF back-testing is annual.

rows.obligation: The institution shall specify conditions, such as major changes in risk profile, credit policies or relevant IT systems, under which the review analyses are performed more frequently than annually.
rows.quote: Ad hoc validation** is performed at the request of the MRC, for example after a significant deterioration of model performance.
rows.rationale: Ad hoc validation exists but is triggered by MRC request, with no specified conditions such as major changes in risk profile, credit policies or IT systems.

rows.obligation: The institution shall review the PD or LGD model whenever it observes a significant change in economic conditions compared with those underlying the model development dataset.
rows.quote: Ad hoc validation** is performed at the request of the MRC, for example after a significant deterioration of model performance.
rows.rationale: Ad hoc validation is possible but no review is required upon a significant change in economic conditions.

rows.obligation: The institution should define a regular cycle for the full review of its rating systems, taking into consideration their materiality.
rows.quote: Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: A regular cycle exists, but it is uniform and does not take materiality into account; tiers only affect depth of work.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure the full review cycle covers all aspects of model development, quantification of risk parameters and, where applicable, the estimation of model components.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Model design and data are covered, but quantification of risk parameters and model components are not clearly included in the review.

rows.obligation: The institution should include in the full review a review of the existing and potential risk drivers and an assessment of their significance based on the predefined standards of review referred to in paragraph 217.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to review risk drivers and assess their significance.

rows.obligation: The institution should include in the full review an assessment of the modelling approach, its conceptual soundness, the fulfilment of the modelling assumptions and alternative approaches.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Model design is covered generally, but conceptual soundness, modelling assumptions and alternative approaches are not explicitly required.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall apply the validation process completely and with adequate frequency.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: Excluding external data and benchmarks, together with PD back-testing only every two years, prevents the validation process from being applied completely and with adequate frequency.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall have an annual validation work plan that is adequate and appropriate.
rows.quote: The annual validation plan is approved by the MRC.
rows.rationale: The policy requires an annual validation plan approved by the MRC, and §4.3 reviews staffing as part of it, which matches the requirement for an annual work plan.

rows.obligation: The institution shall define and document a complete validation process for all rating systems.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: The policy defines initial, regular and ad hoc validation and their content, but it does not set out a complete documented process, for example the steps for IT implementation and consistent application of grades.

rows.obligation: The institution shall perform the validation process with an adequate frequency.
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: Regular validation at least annually for all rating systems in use is an adequate frequency, supplemented by initial and ad hoc validation.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall critically review all aspects of the specification of internal ratings and risk parameters, including data collection and cleansing procedures, methodology and model structure choices, and the variable selection process.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Validation covers design, data and some methodology, but it does not explicitly require critical review of data cleansing procedures, model structure choices or the variable selection process.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall verify the adequacy of the implementation of internal ratings and risk parameters in IT systems.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to verify the implementation of ratings and risk parameters in IT systems.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall verify that grade and pool definitions are consistently applied across departments and geographic areas of the institution.
rows.quote: Validation checks that the same definition of default is applied consistently across models, portfolios and subsidiaries, and in the data used for estimation.
rows.rationale: Consistent application is checked for the default definition and the rating process is assessed, but there is no explicit check that grade and pool definitions are applied consistently across departments and geographic areas.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall verify the performance of the rating systems, taking into account at least risk differentiation, quantification, and the stability of internal ratings, risk parameters and model specifications.
rows.quote: the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability)
rows.rationale: Validation assesses discriminatory power (risk differentiation), calibration (quantification) and stability of the rating distribution.

rows.obligation: The institution shall perform the validation process regularly for all rating systems following an annual work plan.
rows.quote: The annual validation plan is approved by the MRC.
rows.rationale: Regular validation of all rating systems is required annually and an annual validation plan is approved by the MRC.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall perform back-testing for all rating systems at least once annually.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years, using binomial and Jeffreys tests.
rows.rationale: PD back-testing is done only every two years, which is less frequent than the required annual back-testing for all rating systems.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall verify the performance of rating systems covering material types of exposures at least once annually.
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: Performance is validated at least annually for all rating systems in use, which includes those covering material exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its validation methods and procedures allow a consistent and meaningful assessment of the performance of the internal rating and risk estimation systems.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
