rows.rationale: Standard tests and tolerances provide some consistent assessment, but the exclusion of external data and benchmarks and the two-year PD back-testing weaken the meaningfulness of the assessment.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall use validation methods and procedures appropriate for assessing the accuracy and consistency of the rating system.
rows.quote: **Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Methods such as AUC, binomial and Jeffreys tests and back-testing assess accuracy and consistency, but the exclusion of benchmarks limits the appropriateness.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall use validation methods and procedures appropriate to the nature, degree of complexity and range of application of the rating systems and to data availability.
rows.quote: The tier determines the depth of validation work, not whether a model is validated.
rows.rationale: Validation depth varies by tier, but the policy requires no adaptation of methods to the complexity of the rating systems or data availability, and it rules out external data.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall set fixed targets and tolerances for defined metrics, for the initial and regular validation respectively.
rows.quote: PD | AUC (change since initial validation) | ≥ −5 pp | −5 to −10 pp | < −10 pp
rows.rationale: The Annex gives fixed tolerance levels for several metrics, but it does not distinguish targets or tolerances between initial and regular validation.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall apply validation methods, tests, reference data sets and data cleansing consistently over time.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to apply validation methods, tests, reference data sets and data cleansing consistently over time.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall include back-testing and benchmarking in its validation methods.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: Back-testing is required (§8.3, §9.1) but §6.2 explicitly excludes benchmarking, so only half of the obligation is met.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 18
rows.obligation: The validation function should subject all internal models and internal estimates to an initial internal validation and subsequently to an annual internal validation, including new models and material changes and extensions to approved models.
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: Initial and annual validation exist for all rating systems, but material changes and extensions to approved models are not explicitly subject to validation (§3.4 has the Head of Model Development approving them).

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 44
rows.obligation: The institution should review risk estimates when new information comes to light but at least on an annual basis.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Estimates are updated following annual validation, but there is no explicit requirement to review risk estimates when new information comes to light.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 44
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform an annual validation of internal estimates as a basis for the review of estimates (best practice).
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: Annual validation of all rating systems is required, and §16.2 links its results to updating the estimates.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 44
rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit should perform ongoing monitoring as a basis for the review of estimates (best practice).
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention ongoing monitoring by the credit risk control unit as a basis for reviewing estimates.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 48
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform internal validation at all relevant levels.
rows.quote: The Policy applies to the Bank and to all subsidiaries that use the Bank's IRB rating systems.
rows.rationale: The scope includes subsidiaries but the policy does not require validation at all relevant levels (consolidated, sub-consolidated, individual).

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 48
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform validation at least at consolidated level where the rating system is approved on a consolidated basis only.
rows.rationale: No clause requires validation at consolidated level where the system is approved on a consolidated basis.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 48
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform validation at consolidated as well as sub-consolidated and/or individual levels where the rating system is approved at all those levels.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation at consolidated, sub-consolidated and individual levels where approved at those levels.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 48
rows.obligation: The validation function should take the results of sub-consolidated and/or individual level validation into account in the consolidated level validation for consistency.
rows.rationale: There is no requirement to take sub-consolidated or individual-level validation results into account in consolidated validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should assess the performance of rating systems using qualitative and quantitative methods, in particular ranking power and calibration appropriateness.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Validation combines qualitative review (design, data, use) with quantitative assessment of discriminatory power and calibration.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The institution should keep the content of the validation process consistent across rating systems and through time.
rows.quote: The tier determines the depth of validation work, not whether a model is validated.
rows.rationale: A standard validation scope and standard tests (Annex) exist, but there is no explicit requirement to keep validation content consistent across rating systems and over time.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should commensurate the depth of validation analyses and tests to the materiality of the rating systems.
rows.quote: Models are classified into three tiers based on the exposure covered and the risk-weighted exposure amounts. The tier determines the depth of validation work, not whether a model is validated.
rows.rationale: Depth of validation is explicitly scaled to the materiality tier of the model.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should include quantitative analyses with thresholds in the content of the validation process.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Quantitative tests with defined tolerance thresholds are set out in the Annex.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that any statistical tests or confidence intervals used are methodologically appropriate and sufficiently conservative.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years, using binomial and Jeffreys tests.
rows.rationale: Standard statistical tests are specified, but the policy does not require that tests be assessed as methodologically appropriate and sufficiently conservative.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should carry out the validation assessments of rating systems annually.
rows.quote: **Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: Annual validation is required overall, but PD calibration back-testing is only every two years, weakening the annual assessment of calibration.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The institution should define the appropriate frequency of full validations as part of the validation policy.
rows.quote: Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: The policy defines the frequency of regular validation (at least annually) for all rating systems.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform a full validation of material rating systems at least once every three years.
rows.quote: Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use. It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Annual full-scope validation of all rating systems is stricter than the three-year minimum.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform discriminatory power analyses at least at the level of the overall model and, when relevant, at the level of individual risk factors and other segments such as scorecards and modules.
rows.quote: **Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Discriminatory power is assessed (AUC) but no level of analysis is specified, with no requirement for risk factor or segment (scorecard, module) analysis.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 53
rows.obligation: The institution should complete the yearly validation, from reference date of data to approval of results, within no more than one year.
rows.rationale: The policy sets no maximum time from data reference date to approval of the yearly validation results.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 54
rows.obligation: The validation function should set quantitative thresholds for back-testing, discriminatory power, analyses of overrides, and stability analyses of internal ratings and risk parameters over time.
rows.quote: All | Population stability index | < 0.10 | 0.10–0.25 | > 0.25
rows.rationale: Thresholds exist for AUC, Jeffreys, LGD, CCF and PSI, but none for overrides analyses, and the binomial test has no threshold.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 55
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform and document a consistent qualitative assessment of results for tests where no thresholds are applied.
rows.rationale: No requirement for a documented consistent qualitative assessment of tests without thresholds.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution shall review its estimates whenever new information comes to light but at least on an annual basis.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Annual validation exists and estimates are updated on material deficiencies, but there is no explicit estimate review whenever new information comes to light.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should have in place a framework for the review of estimates in line with paragraphs 217 to 221 of the EBA Guidelines on PD and LGD.
rows.rationale: No framework for review of estimates aligned with the EBA PD/LGD guideline provisions is described.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should consider in its frameworks for the review of estimates the availability of data for different exposure types, taking into account model architecture and existing and potential risk drivers.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address data availability across exposure types in a review of estimates framework.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should include in the review framework for material models with statistically based grade assignment, where slight ranking or boundary changes could significantly change RWEA, an analysis of whether including the most recent data in the RDS would lead to materially different model outcomes.
rows.rationale: No analysis of the effect of the most recent data in the RDS is required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should conduct the analysis of the effect of the most recent RDS data on a three-yearly basis, or more often depending on the materiality of the model.
rows.rationale: No three-yearly or materiality-based analysis of the effect of recent RDS data is set out.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should consider in that analysis whether the discriminatory power of the PD or LGD models would be materially increased when re-estimating model parameters on the updated RDS.
rows.rationale: No consideration of discriminatory power gain from re-estimating on the updated RDS.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should have internal validation policies with proven procedures and methods that adequately validate the accuracy, robustness and stability of its estimation of all relevant risk parameters.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: The policy has validation procedures for PD, LGD and CCF, but excluding external data and benchmarks and with only biennial PD back-testing weakens the adequacy of accuracy and robustness validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should align the procedures and methods in its validation policy with its classification of material and non-material rating systems, also considering the complexity of the rating systems.
rows.quote: The tier determines the depth of validation work, not whether a model is validated.
rows.rationale: Tiering sets validation depth by materiality, but complexity of rating systems is not considered and procedures are not explicitly aligned.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should check that the range of application of the model is in line with the approved one, comparing obligor characteristics for PD models and facility types and characteristics for LGD and CCF models.
rows.quote: Each entry records the model owner, developer, scope of application, status, last validation date and open findings.
rows.rationale: Scope of application is recorded and validation covers use of the model, but there is no explicit check of the range of application against the approved one by comparing obligor or facility characteristics.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should assess overrides, not only monitor them, as part of the validation process.
rows.rationale: The policy never mentions overrides, neither monitoring nor assessing them in validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should conduct analyses of overrides on an annual basis (and not at initial validation).
rows.rationale: No annual analysis of overrides is required anywhere in the policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should justify excessive or unexpected variability in the stability of internal ratings and risk parameters over time.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: Stability of the rating distribution is assessed (PSI thresholds), but there is no requirement to justify excessive or unexpected variability, nor stability of risk parameters.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should challenge the model specifications, including assumptions and methodology, based on the applicable regulation.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Model design is covered generally, but there is no explicit challenge of assumptions and methodology against the applicable regulation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should analyse model design stability, including differences between original risk driver weights and weights estimated from a different (longer or more recent) sample, and the continued homogeneity of rating grades or pools used for risk parameter estimation.
rows.rationale: No analysis of design stability, risk driver weight comparison on other samples, or continued homogeneity of grades or pools is required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should justify excessive or unexpected variability in model specifications and design stability.
rows.rationale: No requirement to justify variability in model specifications or design stability.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform model specification and design stability analyses at initial validation and at an adequate frequency thereafter, but at least as part of a full validation.
rows.rationale: No model specification or design stability analyses are required at initial or regular validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should compare model results with up-to-date data from representative and comparable external data sources, in particular for low-default portfolios.
rows.quote: Validation relies on the Bank's internal data only: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: The policy explicitly excludes external data and benchmarks, contrary to the expectation to compare with external data.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should provide sufficient evidence in the event that no usable external data are available for benchmarking.
rows.quote: external data sources and benchmarks are not used, because they are not considered representative of the Bank's portfolios.
rows.rationale: The policy asserts non-representativeness as a blanket statement and requires no evidence that usable external data are unavailable.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform benchmarking analyses at initial validation and at an adequate frequency thereafter, but at least as part of a full validation.
rows.quote: external data sources and benchmarks are not used
rows.rationale: Benchmarking is expressly excluded from initial and regular validation, contrary to the expectation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform quality assurance of the computer codes, including that the implementation of the rating system in the IT system is compliant with and reproduces exactly the documented model under review.
rows.rationale: No quality assurance of code or check of IT implementation against documented model is required of validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform quality assurance of the computer codes at least at initial validation.
rows.rationale: No code quality assurance at initial validation is required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should perform additional qualitative analyses, including assessment of assumptions and expert-based estimates, integrity of the rating assignment process, use of the models and their correct application in practice, legal or macroeconomic changes affecting risk parameters, and downturn phases and correct application of margins of conservatism.
rows.quote: It covers the model design, the data, the quantitative performance (discriminatory power, calibration and stability) and the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Use of the model, the rating process and MoC are covered, but expert-based estimates, legal or macroeconomic changes, downturn phases and correct application in practice are not explicitly required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The institution should have a clear policy defining the appropriate frequency of each qualitative assessment.
rows.quote: Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: A general annual frequency applies to validation overall, but no frequency is defined for each individual qualitative assessment.

rows.obligation: The institution shall make the necessary changes to each rating system following from its assessment.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Requires updating estimates only for material deficiencies, not necessarily the necessary changes to each rating system following from the assessment, and no process or timing is stated.

rows.obligation: The institution shall specifically analyse the reasons for a deviation where realised default rates are outside the expected range for a grade.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Deviations of realised default rates from estimated PDs per grade outside tolerance must be analysed.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have sound internal standards for situations where deviations of realised PDs, LGDs, conversion factors and total losses (where EL is used) from expectations become significant enough to call the validity of the estimates into question.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Tolerance levels exist for PD, LGD and CCF, but there are no standards defining when deviations call validity into question, and total losses are not addressed.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its internal standards for significant deviations take account of business cycles and similar systematic variability in default experience.
rows.rationale: Tolerance levels and deviation standards do not mention business cycles or systematic variability in default experience.

rows.obligation: The institution shall revise estimates upward to reflect its default and loss experience where realised values continue to be higher than expected values.
rows.rationale: No requirement to revise estimates upward when realised values continue to exceed expected values.

rows.obligation: The institution should take into account all relevant deficiencies in methods, processes, controls, data or IT systems identified by the credit risk control unit, validation function, internal audit function or any other internal or external review when identifying and classifying deficiencies.
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A)
rows.rationale: Only deficiencies identified by model developers are considered, not those from the validation function, internal audit, credit risk control unit or other reviews.

rows.obligation: The institution shall develop a plan to rectify data and methodological deficiencies and other sources of additional uncertainty and reduce estimation errors within a reasonable timeframe, considering the materiality of the estimation error and of the rating system.
rows.quote: Each finding has an owner and a remediation deadline: six months for high, twelve months for medium and eighteen months for low findings.
rows.rationale: Findings have owners and deadlines, but there is no plan to rectify data and methodological deficiencies and reduce estimation error considering materiality of the estimation error and rating system.

rows.obligation: The institution shall take appropriate actions, depending on the severity of the deficiency, where material deficiencies are identified through the model change/review procedures.
rows.quote: Where a high finding is not remediated in time, the MRC decides on measures, which may include an additional MoC or restrictions on the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Remediation deadlines and escalation actions are graded by finding severity.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its review framework predefined actions to be taken in case of adverse review results, depending on the severity of the deficiency.
rows.quote: Where a high finding is not remediated in time, the MRC decides on measures, which may include an additional MoC or restrictions on the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Severity-dependent deadlines exist, but actions are predefined only for overdue high findings, and are not predefined for adverse review results generally.

rows.obligation: The institution should take appropriate actions following the results of the review analysis where the review recommends changes to model design.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Updating estimates is addressed, but no action is required on review recommendations to change model design.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have a sound reporting process and a sound process for addressing validation conclusions, findings and recommendations.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: Reporting process plus tracking, quarterly overdue reporting and MRC escalation address the handling of findings.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have a decision-making process ensuring senior management properly takes into account the validation function's conclusions, findings and recommendations, where both units report to the same senior management member.
rows.quote: The **Model Risk Committee (MRC)**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, oversees model risk, approves validation plans and decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The MRC decides on models with open findings, but validation sits under the Head of Model Development and there is no explicit process ensuring senior management takes validation conclusions into account.

rows.obligation: The institution shall decide and implement in a timely manner all corrective measures addressing the validation function's conclusions, findings and recommendations, where both units report to the same senior management member.
rows.quote: Model Validation tracks all open findings in the model inventory and reports overdue findings to the MRC quarterly.
rows.rationale: Deadlines and tracking exist, but timely decision and implementation of corrective measures is enforced only for overdue high findings.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall categorise its findings and recommendations according to their materiality.
rows.quote: Findings are rated *high*, *medium* or *low*.
rows.rationale: Findings are categorised by severity.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have an action plan for each relevant validation recommendation, including follow-up, approved by the appropriate management level.
rows.quote: Each finding has an owner and a remediation deadline: six months for high, twelve months for medium and eighteen months for low findings.
rows.rationale: Owner, deadline and tracking exist, but there is no action plan approved by appropriate management level for each recommendation.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall properly take into account the conclusions, findings and recommendations of the validation function through a decision-making process, where there is no separate validation unit.
rows.quote: Validation is performed by the Model Validation team.
rows.rationale: The bank has a separate Model Validation team, so the rule for institutions without a separate validation unit does not apply.

rows.obligation: The institution shall decide and implement in a timely manner all necessary corrective measures addressing the conclusions, findings and recommendations of the validation function, where there is no separate validation unit.
rows.quote: Validation is performed by the Model Validation team.
rows.rationale: A separate validation unit exists, so the obligation for the case without one does not apply.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall consistently follow up on its own conclusions, findings and recommendations.
rows.quote: Model Validation tracks all open findings in the model inventory and reports overdue findings to the MRC quarterly.
rows.rationale: Validation tracks all its open findings and reports overdue ones, which is consistent follow-up.

rows.obligation: The institution shall reflect the conclusions, findings and recommendations of validation reports in changes and improvements in the design of internal ratings and risk estimates, including in the situations described in the first sentence of Article 185(e) and Article 188(e) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Updating estimates is required only for material deficiencies and covers estimates only, not design changes or improvements from all findings and recommendations.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall take relevant measures where weaknesses of the rating systems are identified by the credit risk control, validation, internal audit or any other control function.
rows.quote: Where a high finding is not remediated in time, the MRC decides on measures, which may include an additional MoC or restrictions on the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Measures are decided only for overdue high findings, and weaknesses identified by credit risk control or other control functions are not covered, though internal audit is addressed separately.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 28
rows.obligation: The institution shall have action plans and related measures for identified weaknesses approved by the audit committee and/or the appropriate management level of the audited areas.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require action plans for internal audit weaknesses to be approved by the audit committee or by management of the audited areas.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 28
rows.obligation: The internal audit shall monitor whether the audited areas implement corrective measures in a timely manner.
rows.rationale: Internal Audit's role in the policy is limited to reviewing the validation team, with no monitoring of corrective measures by audited areas.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 28
rows.obligation: The institution shall use appropriate IT tools to ensure the effectiveness of the monitoring of audit corrective measures.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention IT tools for monitoring audit corrective measures.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 43
rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit should address any deficiencies identified by the validation function.
rows.rationale: The policy has no credit risk control unit and assigns no such unit to address validation deficiencies.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 43
rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit should conduct the approved remediation activities.
rows.rationale: No credit risk control unit is described that conducts approved remediation activities.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should initiate further investigation and, if necessary, trigger adequate measures or actions when validation thresholds are breached.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Threshold breaches trigger analysis and reporting to the MRC, which can then decide measures, though this is stated only for PD back-testing.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 55
rows.obligation: The institution should trigger adequate measures or actions in the event of a negative qualitative assessment.
rows.quote: Where a high finding is not remediated in time, the MRC decides on measures, which may include an additional MoC or restrictions on the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Findings carry owners and deadlines, but the policy does not explicitly trigger measures on a negative qualitative assessment, and the MRC acts only on overdue high findings.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 57
rows.obligation: The institution should be able to demonstrate that measures to remedy identified rating system deficiencies (e.g. model change, recalibration) are initiated on the basis of validation results and recommendations.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Remedial updates are linked to validation results, but only for material deficiencies, and there is no mechanism to demonstrate that model changes or recalibration are initiated from validation recommendations.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 58
rows.obligation: Senior management shall be informed of the status of the measures to remedy any previously identified deficiencies.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The Management Board receives the status of open findings annually, and the MRC receives overdue findings quarterly.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 58
rows.obligation: The institution should have a process in place (e.g. a committee or comparable body) to decide on remedial measures, who is responsible for them, and the implementation timelines, based on validation results and recommendations.
rows.quote: decides on the use of models with open findings.
rows.rationale: The MRC exists and findings have owners and deadlines, but the MRC decides on remedial measures only for overdue high findings, not on remedial measures generally based on validation results.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 58
rows.obligation: The institution should involve persons with appropriate seniority and responsibility from both the CRCU and the validation function in the remediation decision process.
rows.quote: Where a high finding is not remediated in time, the MRC decides on measures, which may include an additional MoC or restrictions on the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Remediation decisions are taken by the MRC, chaired by the CRO, but the policy does not require persons of appropriate seniority from both the credit risk control unit and the validation function to be involved.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 58
rows.obligation: The institution should involve affected business units in the remediation decision process.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require affected business units to be involved in remediation decisions (model owners are only named as finding owners and report recipients).

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 59
rows.obligation: The institution should have adequate processes in place for tracking the status of the measures adopted to remedy deficiencies.
rows.quote: Model Validation tracks all open findings in the model inventory and reports overdue findings to the MRC quarterly.
rows.rationale: The policy sets up tracking of open findings with owners, deadlines and quarterly overdue reporting to the MRC.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should not adapt the model simply to fit singular events from its file review.
rows.rationale: The policy has no provision on avoiding model adaptations that merely fit singular events from a file review.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution shall design review procedures to find and limit errors associated with model weaknesses.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require review procedures to be designed to find and limit errors associated with model weaknesses (no file review or error-limiting procedure is described).

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should provide an overall conclusion on the model so that individual model strengths and weaknesses are evaluated on an overall basis.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The policy mentions an overall assessment of model risk across rating systems but does not require an overall conclusion per model weighing its individual strengths and weaknesses.

rows.obligation: The institution shall assign, and continue to assign, each exposure in the range of application of a rating system to a rating grade or pool of that rating system.
rows.rationale: The duty to assign every exposure within a rating system's range of application to a grade or pool is a rating-system operation obligation, not a validation obligation, and §8.1 only has validation assess the assignment process without requiring completeness of assignment.

rows.obligation: The institution shall provide its own PD estimates for exposures in the exposure classes in points (a) to (d) of Article 147(2), in accordance with Article 143 and Section 6.
rows.quote: The Bank uses own estimates of PD, LGD and CCF for retail exposures and own estimates of PD for corporate exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy states the Bank uses own PD estimates for corporate and retail exposures, which matches the obligation.

rows.obligation: The institution shall estimate PDs by obligor grade from long run averages of one-year default rates for central government, central bank, regional government, local authority, public sector entity, institution and corporate exposures.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: Validation reviews long-run averages of one-year default rates, but it does not mention estimation by obligor grade.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure PD estimates for highly leveraged obligors or obligors whose assets are predominantly traded assets reflect the performance of the underlying assets based on periods of stressed volatilities.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address PD estimates for highly leveraged obligors or obligors with predominantly traded assets, or stressed volatility periods.

rows.obligation: The institution deriving long run average PD and LGD estimates for purchased corporate receivables from an EL estimate shall ensure the process for estimating total losses meets the overall standards for estimation of PD and LGD.
rows.quote: The Bank uses own estimates of PD, LGD and CCF for retail exposures and own estimates of PD for corporate exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy does not show that the Bank holds purchased corporate receivables or derives PD and LGD from an EL estimate for them.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use PD estimation techniques only with supporting analysis.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require supporting analysis for PD estimation techniques.

rows.obligation: The institution shall recognise the importance of judgmental considerations in combining results of techniques and in making adjustments for limitations of techniques and information.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the role of judgmental considerations in combining techniques or in adjusting for their limitations.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall ensure that PD estimates based on internal default experience reflect current underwriting standards and any differences between the rating system that generated the data and the current rating system.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require PD estimates to reflect current underwriting standards or differences between the rating system that generated the data and the current one.

rows.obligation: The institution shall base any mapping of internal grades to an ECAI scale on a comparison of internal rating criteria to the external organisation's criteria and on a comparison of internal and external ratings of any common obligors.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: The policy shows no mapping of internal grades to an ECAI scale.

rows.obligation: The institution shall avoid biases or inconsistencies in the mapping approach or underlying data when mapping internal grades to an external scale.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: The policy shows no mapping of internal grades to an external scale.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the external organisation's criteria underlying the data used for quantification are oriented to default risk only and do not reflect transaction characteristics.
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: The policy shows no use of external organisation data for quantification.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that its use of default probability models to estimate PDs as the simple average of obligor-level estimates in a grade meets the standards specified in Article 174.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: The policy shows no use of default probability models to estimate grade PDs as the simple average of obligor-level estimates.

rows.obligation: The institution shall estimate a PD for each rating grade based on the observed historical average one-year default rate, calculated as an arithmetic average based on the number of obligors (count weighted).
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: The policy mentions long-run averages of one-year default rates but does not require a count-weighted arithmetic average per grade.

rows.obligation: The institution shall not use other averaging approaches, including exposure-weighted averages, to estimate PD per grade.
rows.rationale: The policy does not prohibit other averaging approaches such as exposure-weighted averages.

rows.obligation: The institution shall estimate retail PDs by obligor or facility grade or pool from long run averages of one-year default rates, calculated at facility level only where the definition of default is applied at individual credit facility level.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: Long-run averages of one-year default rates are reviewed, but the policy does not cover retail grade or pool level or facility-level calculation tied to the default definition.

rows.obligation: The institution shall base retail PD on the observed historical average one-year default rate.
rows.quote: Validation reviews whether the PD estimates are long-run averages of one-year default rates.
rows.rationale: The policy covers long-run averages of one-year default rates but does not state that retail PD is based on the observed historical average.

rows.obligation: The institution shall identify and analyse expected changes of risk parameters over the life of credit exposures (seasoning effects) for retail exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to identify or analyse seasoning effects for retail exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall regularly compare realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years, using binomial and Jeffreys tests.
rows.rationale: Grade-level comparison exists but is performed only every two years, which is not sufficiently regular given annual regular validation (§6.2).

rows.obligation: The institution should have a sufficient number of defaulted and non-defaulted observations in the PD model development dataset.
rows.rationale: The sufficiency of defaulted and non-defaulted observations in the development dataset is a model development standard, and the policy's data validation (§7.1) does not address it.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse the market and economic conditions underlying the data for PD estimation in accordance with section 5.3.4.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to analyse the market and economic conditions underlying the PD data.

rows.obligation: Where significant changes in lending standards or recovery policies are observed, the institution should analyse the potential bias in PD estimates in terms of the level of default rates and the likely range of variability of default rates.
rows.rationale: Nothing in the policy addresses bias analysis for changes in lending standards or recovery policies.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in the annual review an analysis of whether including the most recent data materially changes risk estimates, in particular the long-run average default rate for PD and the long-run average LGD or downturn LGD for LGD.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require an annual review analysis of whether the most recent data materially changes the long-run average default rate or LGD.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall ensure its validation methods take account of how business cycles and the related systematic variability in default experience are considered in internal ratings and risk parameters, especially PD estimation.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation methods to consider business cycles and systematic variability in default experience.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 35
rows.obligation: The institution shall report risk profiles and the comparison of estimated PD with realised default rates to senior management more frequently than annually, at least for material rating systems.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Back-testing results reach senior management only annually (and deviations to the MRC), not more frequently than annually as expected.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should design discriminatory power analyses for PD models to ensure the ranking appropriately separates riskier and less risky obligors/facilities.
rows.quote: **Discriminatory power** is assessed annually using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) and its change compared with the initial validation.
rows.rationale: Discriminatory power is assessed via AUC only, with no requirement to design analyses ensuring ranking separates riskier from less risky obligors.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should perform the analysis of predictive power of PD models at grade level, or at a sufficient level of granularity where direct PD estimates are used.
rows.quote: Back-testing compares realised default rates with estimated PDs for each grade every two years
rows.rationale: Predictive power is analysed at grade level as expected.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should use a range of metrics, including statistical tests and graphical analysis of the evolution of default rates and PD, to assess the predictive ability of PD models.
rows.quote: using binomial and Jeffreys tests
rows.rationale: Statistical tests are used but graphical analysis of the evolution of default rates and PD is not required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should define and put in place appropriate actions where internal data are insufficient to establish fixed targets and tolerances for metrics assessing PD model risk differentiation.
rows.rationale: The policy sets fixed tolerances in the Annex and defines no actions where internal data are insufficient to set targets and tolerances; it also excludes external benchmarks (§6.2).

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
rows.obligation: The validation function should analyse the stability of internal ratings and risk parameters over time (e.g. obligor/facility migrations, stability of the migration matrix, concentration in rating grades for PD estimates).
rows.quote: Validation assesses the rating process, the assignment of obligors to grades, and the stability of the rating distribution over time.
rows.rationale: Validation analyses stability of the rating distribution over time, supported by the PSI tolerance in Annex 5, though migration analysis is not explicit.

rows.obligation: The institution shall provide own estimates of LGD, and IRB-CCF where applicable under Article 166(8) and (8b), for retail exposures in accordance with Article 143 and Section 6.
rows.quote: The Bank uses own estimates of PD, LGD and CCF for retail exposures and own estimates of PD for corporate exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy states that own LGD and CCF estimates are used for retail exposures, and §10.1 checks that own CCF estimates are used only where the CRR permits.

rows.obligation: The institution shall provide own estimates of LGD subject to the requirements in Section 6 of Chapter 3 and to permission of the competent authority granted under Article 143.
rows.quote: Exposures to large corporates may migrate to own estimates of LGD where the Bank has at least five years of loss data for that segment and the MRC approves the change.
rows.rationale: The policy ties the migration to own LGD estimates to an MRC approval and a data-history condition, and never mentions the competent authority's permission under Article 143 or the Section 6 requirements.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use an LGD value of 100 % for dilution risk of purchased receivables.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention an LGD of 100% for dilution risk of purchased receivables.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that LGD values used as input to the risk-weighted exposure amount and expected loss formulae for retail exposures are not less than the Table 1 LGD input floors (retail secured by residential property 5 %; QRRE 50 % unsecured; other retail 30 % unsecured; other retail secured by financial collateral 0 %, receivables 10 %, residential or commercial immovable property 10 %, other physical collateral 15 %).
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention LGD input floors for retail exposures or the Table 1 values.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the Table 1 LGD input floors for exposures secured by funded credit protection only where the funded credit protection is eligible under Chapter 3.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address applying LGD input floors only where funded credit protection is eligible.

rows.obligation: The institution shall calculate the applicable LGD input floor for a retail exposure (other than secured by residential property) partially secured by funded credit protection using the formula in Article 161(6).
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the Article 161(6) formula for the LGD floor on partially secured retail exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply an LGD input floor of 5 % to retail exposures secured by residential property irrespective of the level of collateral provided.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the 5% LGD input floor for retail exposures secured by residential property.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply higher LGD input floor values set by the designated authority within a six-month transitional period.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address higher LGD input floors set by the designated authority or the six-month transitional period.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply higher minimum LGD values determined by another Member State's authority to all its corresponding exposures secured by residential or commercial immovable property located in that Member State.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address higher minimum LGD values set by another Member State's authority for property exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution deriving long run average PD and LGD estimates for purchased corporate receivables from an EL estimate shall ensure the outcome is consistent with the concept of LGD in Article 181(1)(a).
rows.quote: The Bank uses own estimates of PD, LGD and CCF for retail exposures and own estimates of PD for corporate exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy shows the bank uses own PD only for corporate exposures and does not mention purchased corporate receivables, so the LGD derivation for them does not apply.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that, where retail long run average PD and LGD are derived from total loss estimates, the process for estimating total losses meets the overall PD and LGD estimation standards and the outcome is consistent with the concept of LGD in Article 181(1)(a).
rows.rationale: The policy does not address deriving retail long-run average PD and LGD from total loss estimates, or requiring consistency with the Article 181(1)(a) LGD concept.

rows.obligation: The institution shall estimate LGDs by facility grade or pool on the basis of the average realised LGDs using all observed defaults within the data sources (default weighted average).
rows.quote: Realised LGDs are compared with estimated LGDs for each pool or grade annually.
rows.rationale: The policy back-tests realised against estimated LGD per pool or grade but does not require a default-weighted average over all observed defaults.

rows.obligation: The institution shall consider the extent of any dependence between the risk of the obligor and the risk of funded credit protection (other than master netting agreements and on-balance-sheet netting of loans and deposits) or its provider when estimating LGD.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to check the dependence between obligor risk and the risk of funded credit protection or its provider.

rows.obligation: The institution shall treat currency mismatches between the underlying obligation and the funded credit protection (other than master netting agreements and on-balance-sheet netting of loans and deposits) conservatively in its assessment of LGD.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the conservative treatment of currency mismatches between the obligation and the protection.

rows.obligation: The institution shall not base LGD estimates that take into account funded credit protection solely on the estimated market value of that protection.
rows.rationale: The policy does not prohibit basing LGD estimates solely on the market value of funded credit protection; §12.1 only requires monitoring of collateral value.

rows.obligation: The institution shall not take into account in LGD estimates any amount expected to be recovered from funded credit protection that it recognises for determining the counterparty credit risk exposure value under Chapter 6, Section 5 or 6.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address excluding recoveries from funded credit protection recognised for counterparty credit risk exposure value from LGD estimates.

rows.obligation: For exposures already in default, the institution shall use the sum of its best estimate of expected loss given current economic circumstances and exposure status and its estimate of the increase of loss rate caused by possible additional unexpected losses during the recovery period.
rows.quote: Validation checks that ELBE reflects current economic circumstances and that LGD in-default exceeds ELBE by an amount that reflects possible additional losses during the recovery period.
rows.rationale: Validation checks that LGD in-default is ELBE plus an add-on for additional unexpected losses during recovery, matching the sum required.

rows.obligation: The institution shall add late payment fees imposed on the obligor before default and capitalised in its income statement to its measure of exposure and loss.
rows.rationale: No clause addresses adding capitalised pre-default late payment fees to exposure and loss measures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall adequately take into account recoveries realised in the course of the relevant recovery processes from any type of funded credit protection and from unfunded credit protection not falling under Article 142(1), point (10).
rows.quote: Validation checks that collateral and guarantees are recognised in LGD estimates only where they meet the Bank's eligibility criteria and that the value of collateral is monitored.
rows.rationale: Validation checks recognition of collateral and guarantees but not that recoveries realised from funded and unfunded protection in recovery processes are adequately taken into account.

rows.obligation: The institution shall address cases with a significant degree of dependence between obligor risk and funded credit protection risk in a conservative manner.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address conservative treatment of dependence between obligor risk and funded credit protection risk.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure LGD estimates take into account the effect of the potential inability to expeditiously gain control of collateral and liquidate it.
rows.rationale: No requirement that validation check LGD reflects the potential inability to expeditiously gain control of and liquidate collateral.

rows.obligation: The institution using own estimates of LGDs and conversion factors shall perform analogous analysis for these estimates.
rows.quote: Realised LGDs are compared with estimated LGDs for each pool or grade annually.
rows.rationale: LGD and CCF back-testing exists, but analogous analysis is not fully specified (e.g. no stability or discriminatory power analysis for LGD and CCF; the policy only covers back-testing and some reviews).

rows.obligation: The institution shall perform the key risk characteristics analysis for LGD models separately for non-defaulted and defaulted exposures.
rows.rationale: The policy has no key risk characteristics analysis for LGD models, separately for defaulted and non-defaulted exposures.

rows.obligation: Where significant changes in lending standards or recovery policies are observed, the institution should analyse the potential bias in LGD estimates in terms of loss rates, average duration of recovery processes, frequencies of use of certain recovery scenarios and loss severity distributions.
rows.rationale: No requirement to analyse LGD bias after significant changes in lending standards or recovery policies.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should design discriminatory power analyses for LGD and CCF models to ensure they discriminate between facilities with high and low LGD or CCF values.
rows.rationale: Discriminatory power analysis is only specified for PD (§8.2); none for LGD or CCF models.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
rows.obligation: The institution should run back-testing of LGD models combining different components (e.g. secured and unsecured) at both component and facility level.
rows.rationale: LGD back-testing is per pool or grade only, with no component-level and facility-level back-testing of combined LGD models.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use SA-CCFs for retail exposures where Article 166(8) and (8b) do not allow the use of IRB-CCF.
rows.quote: checks that own estimates are only used where the CRR permits them
rows.rationale: Validation checks own CCF use is only where CRR permits, but the policy does not require SA-CCFs for retail exposures where IRB-CCF is not allowed.

rows.obligation: The institution shall calculate the exposure value of off-balance-sheet items that are not Annex II contracts using either IRB-CCF or SA-CCFs, in accordance with paragraphs 8a and 8b and Article 151(8).
rows.rationale: Calculating exposure value of off-balance-sheet items is an own funds calculation rule, not a validation policy matter.

rows.obligation: The institution without permission to use IRB-CCF shall calculate the exposure value as the committed but undrawn amount multiplied by the applicable SA-CCF.
rows.rationale: The exposure value calculation with SA-CCF for institutions without permission is a calculation rule belonging in another document.

rows.obligation: The institution that uses IRB-CCF shall calculate the exposure value for undrawn commitments as the undrawn amount multiplied by IRB-CCF.
rows.rationale: Exposure value computation using IRB-CCF is a calculation rule, not a validation policy matter.

rows.obligation: The institution that meets the Section 6 requirements and has competent authority permission shall use IRB-CCF for exposures arising from undrawn revolving commitments under the IRB Approach, provided they would not be subject to a 100% SA-CCF under the Standardised Approach.
rows.quote: checks that own estimates are only used where the CRR permits them
rows.rationale: General check on permitted use of own CCFs, but no mention of revolving commitments, the 100% SA-CCF exception or permission.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use SA-CCFs for all other off-balance-sheet items, in particular undrawn non-revolving commitments.
rows.quote: checks that own estimates are only used where the CRR permits them
rows.rationale: Generic check on permitted use does not specifically require SA-CCFs for non-revolving commitments and other items.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use SA-CCFs for exposures where the Section 6 minimum requirements for calculating IRB-CCF are not met or the competent authority has not permitted IRB-CCF.
rows.quote: checks that own estimates are only used where the CRR permits them
rows.rationale: Generic permitted-use check does not explicitly address unmet Section 6 requirements or lack of authority permission.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that, where IRB-CCF are used solely to calculate RWEA and EL for revolving commitments (other than Article 147(2)(a) exposures), the exposure value is not less than the CCF input floor, being the drawn amount plus 50% of the off-balance exposure amount of the undrawn part calculated using the applicable SA-CCF under Article 111.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention the CCF input floor for revolving commitments.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use the lower of the two conversion factors associated with the individual commitments where a commitment refers to the extension of another commitment.
rows.rationale: No treatment of commitments referring to extension of another commitment or use of the lower CCF.

rows.obligation: Where the institution includes future additional drawings in its conversion factors, it should take them into account in the LGD in both the numerator and the denominator.
rows.rationale: The LGD section does not address treatment of future additional drawings when included in CCFs.

rows.obligation: Where the institution does not include future additional drawings in its conversion factors, it should take them into account in the LGD numerator only.
rows.rationale: The LGD section does not address treatment of future additional drawings in the LGD numerator when excluded from CCFs.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the Article 161(1) LGD values and SA-CCFs under Article 166(8), (8a) and (8b) to exposures to institutions (Art. 147(2)(b)), other financial sector entities and large corporates not in Art. 147(2)(c)(ii), rather than own estimates.
rows.quote: Exposures to large corporates may migrate to own estimates of LGD where the Bank has at least five years of loss data for that segment and the MRC approves the change.
rows.rationale: The policy allows large corporates to migrate to own LGD estimates on an MRC approval, whereas Art. 151(8) requires the Art. 161(1) LGD values for large corporates.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the Article 161(1) LGD values and SA-CCFs to the remaining exposures in Art. 147(2)(a), (aa)(i)/(ii) and (c)(i)-(iii) unless permitted to use own LGD and IRB-CCF estimates under paragraph 9.
rows.quote: Corporate exposures are rated under the foundation approach.
rows.rationale: The policy applies foundation values to corporates and checks that own CCF estimates are only used where the CRR permits, but it does not address the remaining Art. 147(2) classes or the paragraph 9 permission for own LGD and CCF.

rows.obligation: The institution shall establish internal requirements for the management, legal certainty and risk management of funded credit protection taken into account in LGD estimates, generally consistent with those in Chapter 4, Section 3, Sub-section 1.
rows.quote: Validation checks that collateral and guarantees are recognised in LGD estimates only where they meet the Bank's eligibility criteria and that the value of collateral is monitored.
rows.rationale: Validation checks eligibility criteria and collateral value, but the policy does not require internal requirements on management, legal certainty and risk management of funded credit protection.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have clearly specified criteria for the types of guarantors it recognises for the calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts.
rows.quote: Validation checks that collateral and guarantees are recognised in LGD estimates only where they meet the Bank's eligibility criteria
rows.rationale: Eligibility criteria are referred to generically, but the policy does not require clearly specified criteria for the types of guarantors recognised.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply to recognised guarantors the same rules as for obligors set out in Articles 171, 172 and 173.
rows.rationale: Nothing in the policy applies the obligor rules of Articles 171-173 to guarantors.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have clear policies for assessing the effects of unfunded credit protection on risk parameters.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for policies assessing the effects of unfunded credit protection on risk parameters.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its unfunded credit protection policies are consistent with its internal risk management practices and reflect the requirements of Article 183.
rows.rationale: No requirement that unfunded credit protection policies be consistent with risk management practices and Art. 183.

rows.obligation: The institution shall clearly specify in its policies which method of recognising unfunded credit protection is used for each rating system.
rows.rationale: The policy does not specify the unfunded credit protection recognition method per rating system.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply its unfunded credit protection policies consistently over time.
rows.rationale: No requirement to apply unfunded credit protection policies consistently over time.

rows.obligation: The institution shall have clearly specified criteria for adjusting grades, pools or LGD estimates, and for retail and eligible purchased receivables the process of allocating exposures to grades or pools, to reflect the impact of guarantees.
rows.rationale: The policy has no criteria for adjusting grades, pools or LGD estimates, or for the allocation process, to reflect guarantees.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its guarantee adjustment criteria comply with Articles 171, 172 and 173.
rows.rationale: No requirement that guarantee adjustment criteria comply with Articles 171-173.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its guarantee adjustment criteria are plausible and intuitive.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require guarantee adjustment criteria to be plausible and intuitive.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its guarantee criteria address the guarantor's ability and willingness to perform, the likely timing of payments, the correlation between guarantor's and obligor's ability to repay, and the residual risk to the obligor.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the guarantor's ability and willingness to perform, payment timing, correlation or residual risk.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the guarantee requirements of Article 183 also to single-name credit derivatives.
rows.rationale: The policy does not extend guarantee requirements to single-name credit derivatives.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its criteria address the payout structure of the credit derivative and conservatively assess its impact on the level and timing of recoveries.
rows.rationale: The policy has no criteria on the payout structure of credit derivatives or their effect on the level and timing of recoveries.

rows.obligation: The institution shall consider the extent to which other forms of residual risk remain for credit derivatives.
rows.quote: Validation checks that collateral and guarantees are recognised in LGD estimates only where they meet the Bank's eligibility criteria and that the value of collateral is monitored.
rows.rationale: The policy checks eligibility of collateral and guarantees but says nothing about credit derivatives or about considering other forms of residual risk.

rows.obligation: The institution shall not recognise second-to-default and other nth-to-default credit derivatives as eligible unfunded credit protection.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address nth-to-default credit derivatives or their exclusion as eligible unfunded credit protection.

rows.obligation: The institution shall not assign to the covered part of an exposure, under the PD/LGD modelling adjustment approach, a risk weight lower than the protection-provider-RW-floor.
rows.rationale: The policy has no mention of the PD/LGD modelling adjustment approach or a protection-provider risk weight floor for the covered part.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply the guarantee requirements of paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 also to the assignment of retail guarantee exposures to grades or pools and to the estimation of PD.
rows.quote: Validation checks that collateral and guarantees are recognised in LGD estimates only where they meet the Bank's eligibility criteria
rows.rationale: Guarantee eligibility is checked only for LGD estimates, not for the assignment of retail guarantee exposures to grades or pools or for PD estimation.

rows.obligation: The institution shall be more conservative in its estimation the less data it has.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to check that estimates are more conservative where less data is available.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include appropriate adjustments in its estimates, to the extent possible, to overcome biases.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for validation to check appropriate adjustments that correct biases; only MoC is addressed.

rows.obligation: The institution shall, after including appropriate adjustments, add to its estimates a sufficient margin of conservatism related to the expected range of estimation errors.
rows.quote: assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate
rows.rationale: Validation assesses MoC adequacy but only for Category A deficiencies, not the MoC for the expected range of estimation errors in general, and nothing is said about adjustments preceding it.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply a larger margin of conservatism where methods and data are considered less satisfactory and the expected range of errors is larger.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the MoC to scale with the weakness of methods and data or with the size of the expected error range.

rows.obligation: The institution shall add a greater margin of conservatism to its PD estimate, for the expected range of estimation errors not already covered by the appropriate adjustment, where underwriting standards or rating systems have changed.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address a greater MoC for PD where underwriting standards or rating systems have changed (Category B is not covered).

rows.obligation: Where data representativeness is insufficient and leads to bias or increased uncertainty in risk quantification, the institution should introduce an appropriate adjustment to correct the bias.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement on adjusting for insufficient data representativeness.

rows.obligation: Where data representativeness is insufficient and leads to bias or increased uncertainty in risk quantification, the institution should apply a margin of conservatism in accordance with section 4.4.
rows.quote: assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate
rows.rationale: MoC adequacy is reviewed for Category A deficiencies, but representativeness is not linked explicitly, and the policy even excludes external data and benchmarks.

rows.obligation: The institution should identify all deficiencies in the estimation of risk parameters that lead to a bias in quantification or to increased uncertainty not fully captured by the general estimation error.
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A)
rows.rationale: Validation reviews only deficiencies identified by developers in Category A and does not require identifying all deficiencies, including those from increased uncertainty.

rows.obligation: The institution should classify each identified estimation deficiency as Category A (data and methodological deficiencies) or Category B (changes to underwriting standards, risk appetite, collection and recovery policies and other sources of additional uncertainty).
rows.quote: deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A)
rows.rationale: Only Category A is mentioned; Category B (underwriting, risk appetite, recovery policy changes) is not addressed.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse at least all the listed potential sources of additional uncertainty in risk quantification under Category A (e.g. default triggers, date of default, rating assignment, risk driver data, recoveries data, economic loss data, external data representativeness, averaging approach for default rates, downturn information) and Category B (changes to underwriting, collection or recovery policies, portfolio deviations, market or legal changes, forward-looking portfolio changes).
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A)
rows.rationale: Only some Category A sources are touched (data, default definition, cures) and there is no analysis of Category B sources or of the full list such as downturn information and external data representativeness.

rows.obligation: The institution should apply adequate methodologies to correct identified deficiencies to the extent possible, in order to overcome biases in risk parameter estimates.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for methodologies to correct identified deficiencies and overcome biases.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that applying an appropriate adjustment results in a best estimate of the risk parameter.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require that appropriate adjustments yield a best estimate of the parameter.

rows.obligation: The institution should regularly monitor the adequacy of appropriate adjustments.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to monitor the adequacy of appropriate adjustments.

rows.obligation: The institution should not rely on an appropriate adjustment as a replacement for addressing the identified deficiencies.
rows.rationale: The policy does not state that adjustments must not replace addressing the underlying deficiencies.

rows.obligation: The institution should implement a framework for quantification, documentation and monitoring of estimation errors to support the margin of conservatism related to the expected range of estimation errors.
rows.quote: The overall MoC and its components are documented in the model documentation and in the validation report.
rows.rationale: Documentation of the MoC exists, but there is no framework for quantification and monitoring of estimation errors.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure the final MoC reflects the estimation uncertainty in Category A (data and methodological deficiencies), Category B (changes to underwriting, risk appetite, collection and recovery policies and other additional uncertainty) and Category C (general estimation error).
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A) and assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate.
rows.rationale: Only Category A is addressed; Categories B and C and the final MoC reflecting all three are not mentioned.

rows.obligation: The institution should quantify MoC for identified deficiencies, to the extent not covered by the general estimation error, at least for each of categories A and B at the level of the calibration segment.
rows.quote: assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate
