rows.rationale: MoC for Category A is reviewed, but Category B and quantification at calibration segment level are not required.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that, where appropriate adjustments are used, the MoC accounts for any increase in uncertainty or additional estimation error associated with these adjustments.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention appropriate adjustments or MoC accounting for their uncertainty.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that the MoC at category level related to appropriate adjustments is proportionate to the uncertainty around these adjustments.
rows.rationale: No requirement that MoC for appropriate adjustments be proportionate to their uncertainty.

rows.obligation: The institution should apply MoC to address the uncertainty stemming from deficiencies that have not been corrected via appropriate adjustments.
rows.quote: assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate
rows.rationale: MoC for identified Category A deficiencies is reviewed, but uncertainty from deficiencies not corrected by adjustments is not explicitly addressed, nor are other categories.

rows.obligation: The institution should quantify the general estimation error (category C) associated with the underlying estimation method at least for every calibration segment, with the MoC reflecting the dispersion of the distribution of the statistical estimator.
rows.rationale: General estimation error (Category C) quantification per calibration segment is not addressed.

rows.obligation: The institution should quantify the final MoC as the sum of the category A MoC, the category B MoC and the MoC for the general estimation error (category C).
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the final MoC to be the sum of Category A, B and C components.

rows.obligation: The institution should add the final MoC to the best estimate of the risk parameter.
rows.rationale: No requirement that the final MoC be added to the best estimate; §2.4 only defines MoC as an add-on without a validation check.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that the impact of the final MoC does not result in lowering the risk parameter estimates.
rows.rationale: Nothing ensures that the MoC does not lower the risk parameter estimates.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that the MoC stemming from the general estimation error is greater than zero.
rows.rationale: No requirement that the general estimation error MoC be greater than zero.

rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that the MoC for each of categories A and B is proportionate to the increased uncertainty caused by the identified deficiencies in that category and is greater than or equal to zero.
rows.rationale: No requirement of proportionality or non-negativity of Category A and B MoC.

rows.obligation: The institution shall consider the overall impact of identified deficiencies and the resulting final MoC on the soundness of the model.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require considering the overall impact of deficiencies and final MoC on model soundness.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that risk parameter estimates and the resulting own funds requirements are not distorted by the necessity for excessive adjustments.
rows.rationale: No requirement to ensure estimates are not distorted by excessive adjustments.

rows.obligation: The institution shall regularly monitor the levels of the MoC.
rows.quote: The overall MoC and its components are documented in the model documentation and in the validation report.
rows.rationale: MoC is documented in each validation report, but no regular monitoring of MoC levels is required.

rows.obligation: The institution shall not use a MoC as a replacement for addressing the causes of errors or uncertainties or for correcting models to ensure full compliance with Regulation (EU) No 575/2013.
rows.quote: the MRC decides on measures, which may include an additional MoC or restrictions on the use of the model.
rows.rationale: Additional MoC is allowed as a response to unremediated high findings, using MoC as a substitute for addressing causes.

rows.obligation: The institution shall assess the level of the MoC as part of the regular reviews, in particular that the MoC for general estimation error remains appropriate after inclusion of the most recent data relevant for risk parameter estimation.
rows.quote: assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate
rows.rationale: Validation assesses MoC adequacy only for Category A deficiencies and not for general estimation error after including the most recent data as part of regular reviews.

rows.obligation: The institution shall implement necessary changes in the MoC in a timely manner.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require MoC changes to be implemented in a timely manner; §16.2 only says that estimates are updated when material deficiencies are identified.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply a MoC in accordance with section 4.4.3 where material deficiencies are identified through the review procedures.
rows.quote: Where a high finding is not remediated in time, the MRC decides on measures, which may include an additional MoC or restrictions on the use of the model.
rows.rationale: An additional MoC is only an optional measure for overdue high findings, not a requirement to apply a MoC for material deficiencies identified in reviews.

rows.obligation: Where downturn LGD can be calibrated under Section 5 or 6 for only some downturn periods, the model owner shall consider only those estimates and add appropriate Category A MoC under paragraph 37(a) to cover the periods lacking sufficient loss data.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address downturn LGD calibration or a Category A MoC for downturn periods lacking loss data.

rows.obligation: Where a single LGD estimate combines a long-run average and a downturn adjustment, the model owner shall ensure the final MoC encompasses the uncertainties from both the long-run average LGD estimation and the downturn adjustment calculation.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the final MoC to cover uncertainties from both the long-run average LGD and the downturn adjustment.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that the MoC applied to downturn LGD under Section 4.4.3 of the EBA GL on PD and LGD estimation includes a strictly positive Category A MoC to account for the missing data, where it quantifies downturn LGD through any other approach.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for a strictly positive Category A MoC on downturn LGD where other approaches are used.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
rows.obligation: The institution shall add to its risk estimates a margin of conservatism related to the expected range of estimation errors.
rows.quote: the add-on to risk parameter estimates that reflects identified deficiencies and estimation error.
rows.rationale: The policy defines the MoC to include estimation error, but validation only reviews the MoC for Category A deficiencies and does not require a MoC for the expected range of estimation errors.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
rows.obligation: The institution should follow paragraphs 36 to 52 of the EBA Guidelines on PD and LGD when determining the MoC.
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A) and assesses whether the MoC quantified for them is adequate.
rows.rationale: The policy covers only Category A and does not reference or cover the full MoC determination framework (categories B and C, general estimation error, review and timely changes) of paragraphs 36 to 52.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
rows.obligation: The institution shall reflect in the MoC the uncertainty at the level of the final risk estimates (grade or pool).
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the MoC to reflect uncertainty at the level of the final estimates by grade or pool.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
rows.obligation: The institution should be able to ensure monotonicity in its final estimates while still reflecting uncertainty at grade or pool level.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address monotonicity of the final estimates.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
rows.obligation: The institution should consider in the MoC any deficiencies stemming from missing or inaccurate information, including, where relevant and material, missing or inaccurate climate-related information.
rows.quote: Validation reviews the deficiencies identified by the model developers in data and methodology (Category A)
rows.rationale: Data and methodology deficiencies are considered in the MoC, but missing or inaccurate climate-related information is not mentioned and §6.2 excludes external data.

rows.obligation: The institution shall use LGD estimates appropriate for an economic downturn if those are more conservative than the long-run average.
rows.rationale: The policy has no section on downturn LGD or requiring validation to check that downturn-appropriate LGDs are used when more conservative than long-run average.

rows.obligation: The institution shall adjust its risk parameter estimates by grade or pool to limit the capital impact of an economic downturn where the rating system is expected to deliver realised LGDs at a constant level over time.
rows.rationale: Nothing in the policy addresses adjusting estimates to limit the capital impact of a downturn for constant-LGD systems.

rows.obligation: The institution should analyse the market and economic conditions underlying the data for LGD estimation in accordance with section 6.3.2, taking into account the economic downturn required by Article 181(1)(b) CRR.
rows.rationale: The LGD validation section does not mention analysing market and economic conditions underlying LGD data or the downturn.

rows.obligation: The institution shall apply all definitions and requirements in Sections 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the EBA GL on PD and LGD estimation that are relevant when quantifying LGDs appropriate for an economic downturn.
rows.rationale: No requirement to apply the PD/LGD estimation GL definitions when quantifying downturn LGD.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall calibrate downturn LGD at least at the same level at which the corresponding long-run average LGD is calculated for calibrating LGD under paragraph 161 of the EBA GL on PD and LGD estimation.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no requirement on calibrating downturn LGD at least at the long-run average LGD level.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall split the facilities covered by the same LGD model into as many calibration segments as needed where each segment has a significantly different loss profile.
rows.rationale: Calibration segments with different loss profiles for downturn LGD are not addressed.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall at least consider the appropriateness of calibration segments covering material exposure shares in different geographical areas, different industry sectors and, for retail exposures, different product types.
rows.rationale: No consideration of calibration segments by geography, industry or product type is required.

rows.obligation: Where multiple downturn periods are identified, the model owner shall calibrate downturn LGD for each identified downturn period for each calibration segment.
rows.rationale: Multiple downturn periods and per-period calibration are not addressed.

rows.obligation: Where multiple downturn periods are identified, the model owner shall apply the resulting downturn LGD estimates for each period to current non-defaulted exposures at the time of calibration.
rows.rationale: Application of per-period downturn LGDs to current non-defaulted exposures is not addressed.

rows.obligation: Where multiple downturn periods are identified, the model owner shall choose as finally relevant the downturn period resulting in the highest average downturn LGD, including final MoC, on the calibration segment of current non-defaulted exposures.
rows.rationale: Selection of the downturn period with the highest average downturn LGD is not addressed.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall use the downturn LGDs based on the finally relevant downturn period for each calibration segment to comply with Article 181(1)(b) CRR.
rows.rationale: Use of downturn LGDs from the finally relevant period for Art. 181(1)(b) is not addressed.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall provide evidence that the economic factors of a downturn period are not relevant for a calibration segment before omitting downturn LGD calibration for that segment and period.
rows.rationale: No requirement for evidence before omitting downturn calibration for a segment and period.

rows.obligation: Where separate methodologies are used for long-run average LGD and downturn LGD, the model owner shall compare final downturn LGD plus final MoC to long-run average LGD plus final MoC at the level where long-run average LGD is calibrated.
rows.rationale: Comparison of downturn LGD plus MoC with long-run LGD plus MoC is not addressed.

rows.obligation: For models with risk drivers sensitive to the economic cycle, the model owner shall analyse the difference between the current distribution of exposures over facility grades or pools and the likely distribution impacted by the selected downturn period.
rows.rationale: No analysis of exposure distribution over grades or pools under a downturn for cycle-sensitive risk drivers is required.

rows.obligation: Where the analysis shows a substantial difference in distributions, the model owner shall apply an adjustment to downturn LGD estimates to limit the capital impact of an economic downturn.
rows.rationale: No adjustment to downturn LGD for substantial distribution differences is addressed.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall compare the final downturn LGD with the reference value calculated under Section 8 on the relevant RDS, at least at the level of calibration segments.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to compare the final downturn LGD with a reference value on the RDS.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall justify any material difference between the final downturn LGD and the reference value.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to justify differences between the final downturn LGD and a reference value.

rows.obligation: Where a material difference between final downturn LGD and the reference value cannot be justified, the model owner shall re-assess the downturn LGD quantification, ensuring downturn periods are identified comprehensively and impacts on intermediate parameters are aggregated adequately.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address re-assessing the downturn LGD quantification when a material difference cannot be justified.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall use, for downturn LGD estimation for defaulted exposures, the same downturn period as identified for the corresponding non-defaulted exposures.
rows.rationale: The LGD section (§9) does not mention downturn periods, let alone using the same downturn period for defaulted and non-defaulted exposures.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall quantify the downturn component of LGD for defaulted exposures either by calibrating downturn LGD for each reference date or by calibrating at the moment of default and inferring the component at other reference dates, based on the difference from ELBE.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the downturn component for defaulted exposures. §9.2 covers only ELBE and LGD in-default, with no downturn calibration.

rows.obligation: The model owner shall provide evidence of more conservative estimates where it uses the downturn component of non-defaulted exposures instead of that for defaulted exposures at the moment of default.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement for evidence of more conservative estimates when the non-defaulted downturn component is used at default.

rows.obligation: The institution shall calibrate downturn LGD for each considered downturn period using one of the three approaches in Sections 5, 6 and 7 of the guidelines, following the hierarchy in paragraphs 23 to 25.
rows.rationale: The policy contains no downturn LGD calibration approaches or hierarchy.

rows.obligation: The institution shall calibrate downturn LGD for the considered downturn period in accordance with Section 5 where it has sufficient and relevant loss data to conduct the impact analysis in paragraph 27.
rows.rationale: The policy has no mention of downturn calibration based on loss data impact analysis.

rows.obligation: The institution shall calibrate downturn LGD in accordance with Section 6 where sufficient and relevant loss data to assess the impact of the downturn period is not available but calibration under Section 6 is possible.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the Section 6 downturn calibration approach.

rows.obligation: The institution shall calibrate downturn LGD in accordance with Section 7 where sufficient and relevant loss data is not available and quantification under the Section 6 approach is not possible.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the Section 7 downturn calibration approach.

rows.obligation: The institution shall, where the downturn LGD approach involves different intermediate parameters, start aggregating with the parameter showing or estimated to have the highest impact and add any additional impact on other parameters only where necessary.
rows.rationale: The policy has no rules on aggregating the impacts of intermediate parameters for downturn LGD.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that downturn LGD estimates are not biased by observed or estimated cash flows received with a significantly longer time lag than the period referred to in paragraph 156 of the EBA GL on PD and LGD estimation, which might reflect an upturn or improved economic conditions.
rows.rationale: The policy has no check that downturn LGD is unbiased by late cash flows reflecting an upturn. §9.1 covers only incomplete recovery processes and costs.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that downturn LGD estimates including the final MoC are higher than or equal to the minimum of the corresponding long-run average LGDs plus an add-on of 15 percentage points and 105%, where it quantifies downturn LGD through any other approach.
rows.rationale: The policy has no floor for downturn LGD (long-run average plus 15 pp, or 105%).

rows.obligation: The institution shall provide justification to the satisfaction of the competent authority that it cannot calibrate downturn LGD appropriate for the considered downturn period using any of the approaches in Section 5 and Section 6.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to justify to the competent authority that Section 5 and 6 approaches cannot be used.

rows.obligation: Senior management shall notify the management body or its designated committee of material changes or exceptions from established policies that will materially impact the operations of the rating systems.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: Only material changes to rating systems are notified to the MRC (by the Head of Model Development); exceptions from established policies are not addressed.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall regularly inform senior management about the performance of the rating process, areas needing improvement, and the status of efforts to improve previously identified deficiencies.
rows.quote: Model Validation tracks all open findings in the model inventory and reports overdue findings to the MRC quarterly.
rows.rationale: Reporting of findings goes to the MRC and annually to the Management Board, but regular reporting to senior management on rating process performance and improvement areas is not clearly required.

rows.obligation: The institution shall make internal ratings-based analysis of its credit risk profile an essential part of management reporting to the management body and senior management.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Annual validation reporting exists but IRB analysis of the credit risk profile is not made an essential part of management reporting to senior management.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in management reporting at least risk profile by grade, migration across grades, estimation of the relevant parameters per grade, and comparison of realised default rates (and, where own estimates are used, realised LGDs and conversion factors) against expectations and stress-test results.
rows.rationale: No management reporting content on risk profile by grade, migration, parameters per grade or comparison with stress tests is specified.

rows.obligation: The institution shall set reporting frequencies according to the significance and type of information and the level of the recipient.
rows.quote: reports overdue findings to the MRC quarterly
rows.rationale: Some reporting frequencies are set (quarterly, annual) but not according to significance, type of information and recipient level.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall regularly produce and analyse reports on the output of the rating systems.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require regular reports on the output of the rating systems from a credit risk control unit.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall produce and analyse summary reports of the institution's rating systems.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: A summary report across rating systems exists but is produced by Model Validation rather than a credit risk control unit and focuses on validation results.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 81
rows.obligation: The institution shall inform its competent authority of legal impediments to exchanging client data between group entities that result in inconsistencies in the identification of default.
rows.rationale: No requirement to inform the competent authority of legal impediments to data exchange between group entities.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 108
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that internal and external reporting figures reflect a situation where all exposures are correctly classified.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement that internal and external reporting reflect correct classification of exposures.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include the MoC from categories A and B in internal reporting separately for each category, and may reduce it over time and eventually eliminate it once deficiencies are rectified in all affected parts of the rating system.
rows.quote: The overall MoC and its components are documented in the model documentation and in the validation report.
rows.rationale: Only Category A is mentioned and MoC components are documented, without separate internal reporting of categories A and B or the reduction over time.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include the MoC stemming from general estimation error in internal reporting in a separate category ('C').
rows.rationale: No category C MoC for general estimation error is addressed in internal reporting.

rows.obligation: The institution shall provide adequate management reporting on its rating systems.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Validation reporting is present but broader management reporting on rating systems is not defined.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall have defined roles and responsibilities for its staff and senior management and shall submit reports to the management body or its designated committee.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: Reports go to the MRC and the Management Board, but roles and responsibilities of a credit risk control unit's staff and senior management are not defined.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall ensure validation reports identify and describe the validation methods used, the tests performed, the reference data set used and the respective data cleansing processes.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation reports to describe methods, tests, reference data set and data cleansing.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall ensure validation reports include the results of the tests, the conclusions of the validation, the findings and the respective recommendations.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: A report is required for each validation, but its content (test results, conclusions, findings, recommendations) is not specified.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall communicate the conclusions, findings and recommendations of validation reports directly to senior management.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: Validation reports go directly to the MRC and the annual report to the Management Board; the MRC is chaired by the CRO, so senior management receives them directly.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall communicate the conclusions, findings and recommendations of validation reports directly to the management body or the committee designated by it.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Validation results and findings are communicated to the Management Board and to the MRC, the designated committee.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in management reporting the risk profile of obligors or exposures by grade, the migration across grades, and an estimation of the relevant risk parameters per grade.
rows.rationale: The policy has no management reporting content on risk profile by grade, migration across grades or risk parameter estimates per grade.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in management reporting a comparison of realised default rates, and where own estimates are used, of realised LGDs and realised conversion factors, against expectations.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Back-testing of default rates, LGDs and CCFs is reported to the MRC, but the comparison is not required as part of management reporting to senior management, and the PD back-test is only every two years.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in management reporting stress test assumptions and results.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention stress test assumptions or results in any reporting.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in management reporting the performance of the rating process, areas needing improvement and the status of efforts to improve previously identified deficiencies of the rating systems.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Open findings and overdue findings are reported, but the performance of the rating process and areas needing improvement are not explicitly required in management reporting.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include validation reports in management reporting.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: Validation reports are provided to the MRC and summarised for the Management Board.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the form and frequency of management reporting are adequate having regard to the significance and type of the information and the recipient's level in the hierarchy, taking into account its organisational structure.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require that the form and frequency of management reporting be adequate to the significance of the information and the recipient's hierarchy level.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that management reporting facilitates the senior management's monitoring of credit risk in the overall portfolio of exposures covered by the IRB Approach.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement that management reporting facilitates senior management's monitoring of credit risk in the overall IRB portfolio.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that management reporting is proportionate to the nature, size, and degree of complexity of its business and organisational structure.
rows.rationale: There is no statement on proportionality of management reporting to the nature, size and complexity of the business.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall regularly inform the senior management of the performance of the rating systems, of areas needing improvement, and of the status of efforts to improve previously identified deficiencies.
rows.quote: Model Validation tracks all open findings in the model inventory and reports overdue findings to the MRC quarterly.
rows.rationale: Findings status is reported quarterly to the MRC and annually to the Management Board, but regular reporting on rating system performance and areas needing improvement is not explicitly required, and the unit is not described as the credit risk control unit.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should have procedures for internal and external model risk communication and reporting.
rows.quote: As a significant institution, the Bank reports the results of the annual validation of its IRB models to the ECB in line with the ECB's reporting instructions.
rows.rationale: Internal reporting and external reporting to the ECB are defined for validation results, but no general procedures for model risk communication are set out.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 17
rows.obligation: The senior management should either report directly to the management body or be responsible for providing it with the necessary information to carry out its duties, especially its oversight role.
rows.rationale: The relationship between senior management and the management body is a general governance matter and not for a model validation policy.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 28
rows.obligation: The institution shall prepare regular (at least annual) status reports on internal audit follow-up actions and discuss the results in the appropriate committees.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require regular status reports on internal audit follow-up actions to be discussed in committees.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 28
rows.obligation: The institution shall submit to the competent authority a summary of the outcomes of the relevant audit reports, action plans and the status of findings.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require submission of a summary of audit report outcomes, action plans and findings status to the competent authority; §14.3 covers only validation results.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 24
rows.obligation: The institution shall communicate the materiality of its rating systems to the competent authority.
rows.quote: the Bank reports the results of the annual validation of its IRB models to the ECB in line with the ECB's reporting instructions.
rows.rationale: The policy reports validation results to the ECB but does not state that the materiality of rating systems is communicated to the authority.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 32
rows.obligation: The institution shall provide management reporting on the performance of its rating systems.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The policy requires management reporting on the performance of the rating systems through validation reports to the Management Board and the MRC.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 33
rows.obligation: The institution shall determine the level of detail of information and data, and the frequency of reporting, to be presented to senior management and the management body.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Frequency and content are set for the Board and MRC reports, but there is no determination of the level of detail for senior management and no distinction by audience.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 33
rows.obligation: The institution shall clearly define in its policies the reporting procedures for non-material rating systems and clearly identify differences from reporting for material rating systems.
rows.rationale: The policy defines no separate reporting procedures for non-material rating systems and no differences from material ones; the tiers only drive validation depth.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 34
rows.obligation: The institution shall include in management reports the materiality of each rating system, its perceived strengths and limitations, and its current status in the light of validation and/or audit actions.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: Open findings (status per validation) are reported, but the materiality of each rating system and its strengths and limitations are not required.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 35
rows.obligation: The institution shall provide reports to the management body that are more concise than reports to senior management while including the information necessary for sound and appropriate decision-making.
rows.rationale: The policy does not differentiate between the conciseness of reports to the management body and to senior management.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 35
rows.obligation: The institution shall provide reports to senior management as often as, or more frequently than, to the management body.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: The MRC receives reports at least as often as the Board (every validation, quarterly overdue findings versus annual), but this is not stated as a principle and the MRC's role as senior management is not made explicit.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 36
rows.obligation: The institution shall provide both senior management and the management body, at least annually, with an aggregated overview of the validation results for each rating system.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The annual aggregated results go to the Management Board, but the MRC/senior management receives per-validation reports; the annual aggregated overview is stated only for the Board.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting includes information on the risk profile of obligors or exposures by grade.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require management reporting on the risk profile of obligors or exposures by grade.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting includes information on migration across grades.
rows.rationale: Grade migration is not required in management reporting; only rating distribution stability is assessed in validation (§8.1).

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting includes an estimation of the relevant risk parameters per grade.
rows.rationale: No requirement for management reporting of estimated risk parameters per grade.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting includes a comparison of realised default rates, and, where own estimates are used, of realised LGDs and realised conversion factors against expectations.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Back-testing of default rates, LGDs and CCFs is performed and PD deviations are reported to the MRC, but management reporting of the comparison against expectations is not explicitly required for all parameters.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting includes stress test assumptions and results.
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention stress test assumptions and results in management reporting.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting includes the performance of the rating process, areas needing improvement and the status of efforts to improve previously identified deficiencies of the rating systems.
rows.quote: Model Validation tracks all open findings in the model inventory and reports overdue findings to the MRC quarterly.
rows.rationale: Open findings and remediation status are reported, but the performance of the rating process and areas needing improvement are not explicitly required in management reporting.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting includes validation reports.
rows.quote: Model Validation prepares a validation report for every validation, addressed to the model owner and the MRC.
rows.rationale: Validation reports are provided to the MRC (senior management) and summarised for the Management Board.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the form and frequency of management reporting are adequate having regard to the significance and type of the information and the recipient's level in the hierarchy, taking into account the organisational structure.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The policy sets differentiated reporting by recipient (per-validation reports to owner and MRC, annual summary to the Management Board, quarterly overdue findings to the MRC), but it does not require that form and frequency be assessed for adequacy against significance, type of information and hierarchy level.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 37
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure management reporting facilitates senior management's monitoring of credit risk in the overall portfolio of exposures covered by the IRB Approach.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The annual aggregated report supports senior management's oversight of the rating systems, but the policy does not explicitly address monitoring credit risk across the overall IRB portfolio, and the reporting is only annual.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 53
rows.obligation: The institution should report deviations from the one-year yearly validation duration to senior management.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement to report deviations from the annual validation cycle to senior management; it only requires annual validation and reports overdue findings.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 56
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure that senior management and the management body (or its designated committee) are informed of validation conclusions and recommendations, in particular exceeded thresholds and deficiencies identified.
rows.quote: Deviations outside the tolerance levels in the Annex are analysed and reported to the MRC.
rows.rationale: Validation reports go to the MRC and the Management Board gets an annual summary, but only PD calibration threshold breaches are explicitly reported (to the MRC), and exceeded thresholds for other tests are not required to be reported to senior management.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 56
rows.obligation: The validation function should, where appropriate, provide validation information in summary documents presenting an aggregated view and comparison of results for all rating systems.
rows.quote: An annual validation report summarising the results for all rating systems, open findings and the overall assessment of model risk is presented to the Management Board.
rows.rationale: The annual summary report presents aggregated results for all rating systems, though comparison across systems is not explicit.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall review and document any changes to the rating process, including the reasons for the changes.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the credit risk control unit (validation) to review and document changes to the rating process and their reasons.

rows.obligation: The credit risk control unit shall carry out ongoing review and alterations to models used in the rating process.
rows.quote: Regular validation** is performed at least annually for all rating systems in use.
rows.rationale: Annual validation gives an ongoing review, but the policy does not require ongoing review and alteration of the models by the control unit.

rows.obligation: The institution shall specify internal policies for changes of models and estimates of risk parameters used within a rating system.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: Only an approval step for material changes is set out; there is no real internal policy for changes of models and estimates of risk parameters.

rows.obligation: The institution shall provide in its model change policies that model changes are made as a result of at least regular review of estimates, independent validation, changes in the legal environment, internal audit review and competent authority review.
rows.quote: Model owners update the estimates of their models when validation identifies material deficiencies.
rows.rationale: Only validation findings are named as a trigger for changes; regular review of estimates, legal changes, internal audit and competent authority reviews are not covered.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall have a role in the internal approval procedure of rating systems and all related changes.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: Material changes are approved without any validation involvement, although new systems are approved by the MRC after initial validation; validation has no role in approving changes.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall verify all changes relating to internal ratings and risk parameters and their materiality in accordance with Delegated Regulation (EU) No 529/2014.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation to verify changes to ratings and risk parameters or their materiality under Delegated Regulation 529/2014.

rows.obligation: The validation function shall perform the validation of specification review, IT implementation and performance before a rating system is used for own funds requirements and internal risk management, when the institution applies for permission to use it or for material changes to it.
rows.quote: Initial validation** is performed for every new rating system before the Bank applies for permission to use it or before its first use for own funds requirements.
rows.rationale: Initial validation is required for new systems, but not for material changes, and IT implementation is not mentioned.

rows.obligation: The institution shall properly implement its change policy for changes to the range of application of rating systems and to the rating systems themselves, in line with Articles 2 to 5, Article 8 and Annex I of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 529/2014.
rows.rationale: The policy has no change policy implementing Delegated Regulation 529/2014 for changes to the range of application or to rating systems.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure its change policy implements the requirements of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and the criteria in Articles 1 to 5, Article 8 and Annex I of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 529/2014, and provides for their practical application.
rows.rationale: The policy does not contain a change policy implementing the CRR requirements and Delegated Regulation 529/2014 criteria.

rows.obligation: The institution shall set out in its change policy the responsibilities, reporting lines and procedures for the internal approval of changes, having regard to its organisational characteristics and approach specificities.
rows.quote: Material changes to rating systems are approved by the Head of Model Development, who informs the MRC at its next meeting.
rows.rationale: Approval responsibility is set for material changes only, without full reporting lines and procedures for internal approval of all changes.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its change policy definitions, methods and, where applicable, metrics for the classification of changes to rating systems.
rows.rationale: The policy gives no definitions, methods or metrics for classifying changes; it only mentions 'material changes' without defining them.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its change policy procedures to identify changes to rating systems.
rows.rationale: No procedures to identify changes to rating systems are set out.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its change policy procedures to monitor changes to rating systems.
rows.rationale: No procedures to monitor changes to rating systems are set out.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its change policy procedures to notify changes to rating systems to competent authorities.
rows.rationale: No procedure to notify competent authorities of changes to rating systems is set out.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its change policy procedures to apply for permission on changes to rating systems from competent authorities.
rows.rationale: No procedure to apply for competent authority permission on changes to rating systems is set out.

rows.obligation: The institution shall include in its change policy procedures for the implementation of changes to rating systems.
rows.rationale: A change policy with procedures for implementing rating system changes belongs in a separate model change policy, not in this validation policy, whose scope is validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 79
rows.obligation: The institution shall implement an approved material model change or extension within no longer than three months from the date of notification of the permission.
rows.rationale: The three-month implementation deadline after permission notification is a change-implementation obligation for a model change policy, not a validation matter.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 79
rows.obligation: The institution shall request any exception to the three-month implementation time frame as early as possible, no later than when submitting comments in the model decision process, and give reasons.
rows.rationale: Requesting exceptions to the implementation time frame is part of change management and supervisory dialogue, not validation.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 30
rows.obligation: The management body and senior management shall be responsible for the quality of applications and notifications and for the timeliness of their submission and implementation of new models, model changes or extensions.
rows.rationale: Management responsibility for application quality and timeliness of model changes belongs in a governance or change policy; the validation policy only covers approval roles.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 31
rows.obligation: The institution shall only submit applications for approval of new models, model changes or extensions once all changes needed to remediate deficiencies of the rating system have been made.
rows.rationale: Submitting applications only after remediating deficiencies is a change and application process obligation, not covered by validation scope.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 52
rows.obligation: The validation function should conduct initial validation of new models and of material changes and extensions to approved models, covering the aspects directly or indirectly affected by the change.
rows.quote: **Initial validation** is performed for every new rating system before the Bank applies for permission to use it or before its first use for own funds requirements.
rows.rationale: Initial validation covers new rating systems only, while material changes and extensions are approved by the Head of Model Development without any requirement for initial validation of the affected aspects.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 60
rows.obligation: The institution should always apply to or notify the competent authority of changes to its validation methodology and/or processes in accordance with Annex 1 Part 2 Section 1 (material model change) or Section 2 (ex ante notification) of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 529/2014.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require applying to or notifying the competent authority of changes to the validation methodology or processes.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: Internal audit should include in its general risk assessment its opinion on the materiality classification process, impact assessment and regulatory compliance of all rating system changes and their implementation.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: Internal audit reviews the validation team but is not required to give an opinion on the materiality classification, impact assessment and compliance of rating system changes.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: The institution should ensure internal audit is informed of all changes to the rating systems.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require that internal audit be informed of changes to rating systems.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 67
rows.obligation: The institution shall submit reports of its independent review or validation together with the application for extensions and changes to the IRB approach.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require validation reports to be submitted with applications for IRB extensions and changes; §14.3 only covers annual reporting to the ECB.

rows.obligation: Internal audit or another comparable independent auditing unit shall review the institution's rating systems and their operations, including the credit function and the estimation of PDs, LGDs, ELs and conversion factors, at least annually.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan
rows.rationale: The policy sets a three-year review cycle, whereas Art. 191 requires at least annual review of rating systems, and the review is of the validation team rather than the rating systems.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall include adherence to all applicable requirements in its areas of review.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require Internal Audit to include adherence to all applicable requirements in its review.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 114
rows.obligation: The internal audit unit or another comparable independent auditing unit should regularly review the robustness and effectiveness of the default identification process, taking into account timeliness of identification of default.
rows.rationale: Nothing requires Internal Audit to review the default identification process or the timeliness of default identification.

rows.source: EBA GL definition of default (GL/2016/07) para. 114
rows.obligation: The internal audit unit should communicate its review conclusions and recommendations, and the measures taken to remedy identified weaknesses, directly to the management body or its designated committee.
rows.rationale: The policy does not say Internal Audit communicates conclusions, recommendations and remedial measures to the management body or its committee.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall fulfil its required role in accordance with Article 17.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan
rows.rationale: The internal audit role under Art. 17 requires annual review of rating systems, but the policy only provides a three-yearly review of the validation team.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall regularly assess the fulfilment of the resourcing, remuneration, decision-making, undue-influence and corrective-measure conditions, where validation and credit risk control units report to the same senior management member.
rows.quote: reports to the Head of Model Development, with a dotted reporting line to the Chief Risk Officer for validation matters
rows.rationale: The policy shows no shared senior management member for validation and the credit risk control unit, so this condition is not triggered.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall have an adequate and appropriate annual internal audit work plan, auditing manuals and work programs, and an action plan with follow-up for each relevant recommendation approved at the appropriate management level.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan
rows.rationale: The policy mentions an audit plan but not an annual work plan, audit manuals, work programs or an action plan with follow-up of recommendations.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall regularly assess the fulfilment of the conditions on resources, remuneration, decision-making, undue influence and corrective measures for the validation function, where there is no separate validation unit.
rows.quote: including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports
rows.rationale: The validation function is part of the development department, so no separate unit exists and the audit must assess the conditions regularly, but the policy only provides a three-yearly review of independence, methods and report quality, without resources, remuneration, decision-making, undue influence or corrective measures.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall review all rating systems of the institution at least annually.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan
rows.rationale: The review is three-yearly and targets the validation team, not all rating systems annually.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall review the operations of the credit risk control function at least annually.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require Internal Audit to review the credit risk control function.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall review the operations of the credit approval process at least annually.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require Internal Audit to review the credit approval process.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall review the operations of the internal validation function at least annually.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years
rows.rationale: The validation function is reviewed every three years instead of at least annually.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall ensure its review facilitates specifying in the annual work plan the areas requiring a detailed review of compliance with all IRB requirements in Articles 142 to 191 of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require the audit review to identify areas needing detailed compliance review against Arts. 142 to 191 in an annual work plan.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that internal audit or the other comparable independent auditing unit is functional and adequate for its tasks.
rows.quote: including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports
rows.rationale: Internal Audit reviews the validation function's quality, but the policy has no requirement that the audit function itself is functional and adequate.

rows.obligation: Internal audit shall provide sufficient information to the senior management and the management body on the compliance of the rating systems with all applicable IRB requirements.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require Internal Audit to report to senior management and the management body on rating system compliance with IRB requirements.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that internal audit is proportionate to the nature, size and degree of complexity of its business and organisational structure, in particular to the complexity of the rating systems and their implementation.
rows.rationale: §15.1 sets a fixed three-year review of Model Validation only and says nothing about proportionality of internal audit to the nature, size and complexity of the business and rating systems.

rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure that internal audit has adequate resources and experienced and qualified personnel to undertake all relevant activities.
rows.rationale: The policy does not address the resources, experience or qualifications of internal audit personnel.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 21
rows.obligation: Internal audit should regularly assess whether the additional independence requirements under option (b) are being met.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: Internal audit reviews validation independence, but only every three years and not specifically the additional option (b) requirements, so this is not a regular assessment.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 22
rows.obligation: The internal audit shall regularly assess that the additional requirements for the validation function option (c) are met (best practice under Article 22(2) of the Final draft RTS).
rows.rationale: The policy does not mention validation function option (c) or any internal audit assessment of its additional requirements; §15.1 only gives a general independence review.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 25
rows.obligation: The internal audit shall regularly review internal models, and the review shall be efficient and effective.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: Internal audit reviews only the validation team every three years, not the internal models themselves regularly, and says nothing on efficiency or effectiveness.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 26
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure the internal audit is effectively separated from the staff involved in the operations of the internal models, e.g. the validation function, the risk control unit and other relevant business areas.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require internal audit to be separated from staff operating the models, such as the validation function.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 26
rows.obligation: The internal audit shall report directly to the management body.
rows.rationale: The policy does not state that internal audit reports directly to the management body.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 26
rows.obligation: The institution shall ensure no undue influence is exerted on the staff responsible for internal audit conclusions.
rows.rationale: The policy has no provision protecting internal audit conclusions from undue influence.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 27
rows.obligation: The internal audit shall have adequate resources and experienced, qualified personnel with appropriate quantitative and qualitative knowledge to undertake all relevant activities.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement on internal audit resources or on the quantitative and qualitative knowledge of its staff.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 27
rows.obligation: The internal audit shall be adequately equipped and managed in proportion to the nature, size and complexity of the institution's business and organisational structure.
rows.rationale: The policy has no requirement that internal audit be equipped and managed in proportion to the institution's size and complexity.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 28
rows.obligation: The internal audit shall report its conclusions, findings and recommendations to the audit committee and/or the appropriate management level of the audited areas.
rows.rationale: The policy does not say to whom internal audit reports its conclusions, findings and recommendations.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 61
rows.obligation: Internal audit shall review the institution's rating systems and their operations at least annually.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan
rows.rationale: A three-year cycle limited to the validation team is incompatible with an at least annual review of the rating systems and their operations.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 61
rows.obligation: Internal audit shall include adherence to all applicable requirements in the areas it reviews.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require internal audit to cover adherence to all applicable requirements in the areas it reviews.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 62
rows.obligation: Internal audit should carry out annually, on up-to-date information, a general risk assessment of all aspects of the rating systems to draw up the audit work plan, and execute that plan.
rows.rationale: The policy has no annual general risk assessment of the rating systems to draw up the audit work plan.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 63
rows.obligation: Internal audit should subject areas showing signs of increased/high risk in the general risk assessment to a thorough audit assignment (deep dive) and include these in the annual audit work plan.
rows.rationale: The policy has no deep-dive audits of high-risk areas in the annual audit work plan.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 63
rows.obligation: Internal audit should perform a deep dive on areas not showing increased/high risk at least every three years.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: The policy sets a three-year review cycle but only for the Model Validation team, not for the rating systems and their areas as a deep dive on non-high-risk areas.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: Internal audit should develop its own opinion on the areas of the rating systems to be reviewed in the general risk assessment.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require Internal Audit to form its own opinion on the areas of the rating systems to be reviewed in a general risk assessment.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: Internal audit should include in its general risk assessment its opinion on the development and performance of the rating systems.
rows.rationale: No requirement for Internal Audit to include an opinion on the development and performance of rating systems in a general risk assessment.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: Internal audit should include in its general risk assessment its opinion on the quality of the data used for the quantification of risk parameters.
rows.rationale: No requirement for Internal Audit to give an opinion on the quality of data used for risk parameter quantification.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 64
rows.obligation: Internal audit should include in its general risk assessment its opinion on the integrity of the rating assignment process.
rows.rationale: No requirement for Internal Audit to give an opinion on the integrity of the rating assignment process.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 65
rows.obligation: Internal audit should properly document the general risk assessment and prioritisation procedures and results, the annual work plan, the guidelines and the audit reports, and have them approved by the management body.
rows.rationale: The policy does not require documentation of Internal Audit's risk assessment, work plan, guidelines and reports, or their approval by the management body.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 67
rows.obligation: Internal audit should independently assess the review of material changes in validation methodology and/or processes, or process-related aspects of changes in the definition of default.
rows.quote: Internal Audit reviews the Model Validation team every three years as part of the audit plan, including its independence, methods and the quality of its reports.
rows.rationale: Internal Audit reviews validation methods generally, but there is no requirement to independently assess the review of material changes in validation methodology or processes, or process aspects of default definition changes.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 12
rows.obligation: The institution should maintain a register of its internal models that facilitates a holistic understanding of the application and use of the models and gives the management body and senior management a comprehensive overview of the models in place.
rows.quote: All IRB models are recorded in the model inventory, maintained by Model Validation. Each entry records the model owner, developer, scope of application, status, last validation date and open findings.
rows.rationale: A model inventory with key attributes exists, but the policy does not state that it gives the management body and senior management a comprehensive overview, and it covers only IRB models.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 13
rows.obligation: The institution should subject each internal model to a regular complexity assessment.
rows.rationale: The policy has tiering by exposure and RWA (§5.2) but no regular complexity assessment of models.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 13
rows.obligation: The institution should be able to classify its internal models based on their complexity.
rows.quote: Models are classified into three tiers based on the exposure covered and the risk-weighted exposure amounts.
rows.rationale: Models are classified into tiers, but on materiality (exposure and RWA) rather than on complexity as expected.

rows.source: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles for internal models, para. 13
rows.obligation: The institution should clearly identify internal models to be labelled as highly complex (e.g. due to the use of ML techniques) or dynamic.
rows.rationale: The policy does not identify highly complex (e.g. ML) or dynamic models.
